skills.body:
---
name: android-cli
description: Provides instructions for installing and using the `android` CLI. The
  `android` command-line tool is a critical tool for Android development and helps
  you create new Android projects, install APKs onto devices and emulators and launch
  and run apps on them, manage and interact with Android virtual devices (including
  screenshots and UI inspection), manage Android SDK components, inspect built artifacts
  (APK, AAB, JAR, AAR) for build and optimization details, render Compose previews,
  look up official Android documentation, and discover and install official Android
  skills.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
metadata:
  author: Google LLC
  last-updated: '2026-11-14'
  keywords:
  - android-cli
  - sdk
  - emulator
  - skills
  - docs
  - knowledge base
  - project creation
  - screenshots
  - apk analysis
  - compose preview
---

This skill provides instructions for using the `android` CLI tool. The tool
includes various commands for creating projects, running applications,
interacting with devices, and managing the CLI environment.

## Installation

If the android tool is not in the path, install it. To install run the following
command:

- Linux x86-64: curl -fsSL https://dl.google.com/android/cli/latest/linux_x86_64/install.sh \| bash
- Linux ARM64: curl -fsSL https://dl.google.com/android/cli/latest/linux_arm64/install.sh \| bash
- Mac Arm: curl -fsSL https://dl.google.com/android/cli/latest/darwin_arm64/install.sh \| bash
- Mac Intel: curl -fsSL https://dl.google.com/android/cli/latest/darwin_x86_64/install.sh \| bash
- Windows: curl -fsSL https://dl.google.com/android/cli/latest/windows_x86_64/install.cmd -o "%TEMP%\\i.cmd" \&\& "%TEMP%\\i.cmd"

## SDK management

To manage the installation of Android SDKs and tools, use the `sdk` command.
For example:

- `android sdk install <package>[@<version>]...`: Install specific packages. Multiple packages can be specified, separated by spaces. `<version>` defaults to latest. For example: `android sdk install platforms/android-30@2
  platforms/android-34`
- `android sdk update [<pkg-name>]`: Update a specific package or all packages to the latest version.
- `android sdk remove <pkg-name>`: Remove a package from the local SDK.
- `android sdk list --all`: List installed and available SDK packages.

## Project creation

Create projects from templates using the `create` command.

For example: `android create empty-activity --name="My App" --output=./my-app`

## Interacting with Android devices

Use the `android layout` command to inspect the UI layout of an Android
application in JSON format. Use the `android screen` command to visually inspect
the UI and obtain bounding coordinates for visual regions.
`android layout` dumps the UI as JSON. `android screen capture -o <file path>` saves a PNG.
Both auto-select the device when only one is connected; with more than one, pass `--device=<serial>` (use `adb devices` to list serials).

### UI Dump

`android layout` returns a JSON tree of the UI elements on screen.

Each JSON object represents a UI element in the Android app. The following properties may be present:
- `text` - any literal text the element contains
- `resource-id` - the Android resource id used to refer to the element
- `content-desc` - a description of a UI element for use by accessibility tools
- `interactions` - the set of user interactions the element supports. May contain one or more of: `CHECKABLE`, `CLICKABLE`, `FOCUSABLE`, `SCROLLABLE`, `LONG-CLICKABLE`, `PASSWORD`
- `state` - the set of states the element is in. May contain one or more of `CHECKED`, `FOCUSED`, `SELECTED`
- `bounds` - the screen coordinates of the bounding rectangle of the element, in the format `[min X,min Y][max X, max Y]`
- `center` - the screen coordinates of the center of the element, in the format `[x,y]`
- `off-screen` - if true, the element is in the UI hierarchy but not within the bounds of the screen; it may require scrolling to view.
- `hidden` - if true, the element is in the UI hierarchy but not visible or interactive on screen.

Use `layout` as a primary means of examining an Android app.

By default, `layout` only returns elements that have content or are interactive:
- elements with non-empty `text` or `content-desc` properties
- elements with non-empty `interactions` or `state`
To return all elements, use the `--full` flag

If `layout` continues to fail, use `android screen capture --annotate` to inspect the app.

### Screenshot

`android screen capture -o <file path>` (or `--output=<file path>`) saves a PNG of the current device screen to `<file path>`.

Use `screen capture` as a secondary means of examining an Android app
Examples:
- Understanding the content of an on-screen image
- Looking at a `WebView` (web content does not always appear in the ui dump)
- Trying to find a UI element by its visual appearance

**IMPORTANT** : Always *VISUALLY* examine the PNG image returned from any `android screen` command BEFORE doing anything else.

#### Annotated Screenshot

`android screen capture --annotate -o <file path>` (or `-a -o <file path>`)
`android screen resolve --screenshot <path> --string <string>`

The `--annotate` command adds numerical labels and bounding boxes around UI elements. Use this command to locate UI elements that cannot
be located in the `layout` output.

To refer to these labels in input commands, use `screen resolve` to convert labels into coordinates:

`android screen resolve --screenshot <file path> --string "#3"` returns `<x coord of region 3> <y coord of region 3>`

To save turns, you can combine shell commands:

`adb shell input $(android screen resolve --screenshot screen.png --string "tap #34")`

This command taps on region #34 from `screen.png`

### Input

Use `adb shell input` for interacting with Android devices.
Refer to the `"interactions"` property of an element for what interactions can be performed on a particular element.

Interact with UI elements with their `center` coordinate or their `bounds` coordinates:
`json
{
"key": -248568265,
"class": "android.widget.Button",
"bounds": "[138,9][167,38]",
"center": "[152,23]"
}`
To tap on this button, you would execute `adb shell input tap 152 23`. This taps the center.

```json
{
  "key": 12487234,
  "class": "com.example.ui.ScrollableList",
  "bounds": "[100,200][400,600]",
  "center": "[250,400]"
}
```

To scroll down on this list, you would execute `adb shell input swipe 250 400 250 200 500`. This swipes from the center to the top over 500ms.

#### Text Input

To enter text, ensure the field is focused and execute `adb shell input text "<text>"`.

- **Spaces (`%s`):** Replace spaces with `%s` (Android ignores text after raw spaces): `adb shell input text "Hello%sworld"` (enters `"Hello world"`).
- **Special characters:** Escape shell metacharacters (`&`, `$`, `(`, `)`, `!`): `adb shell input text "AT\&T"` or `adb shell input text 'Price:\$10'`.
- **Submit / Enter:** `adb shell input keyevent 66`

### Android Interaction Rules

1. Always ensure text input fields have `"FOCUSED"` in their `"state"` list before entering text.
2. If an element has `"SCROLLABLE"` in its `"interactions"` list, try scrolling it when looking for missing UI elements.
3. Always scroll slowly when executing scroll inputs. The 5th argument to `adb shell input swipe` controls scroll duration.
4. Content may take time to load; if a `layout` is missing information after you take an action, wait a few seconds, then perform `layout` again to see if anything changes.

## Running journey tests

Journey tests involve device interaction; use the `android layout` and `android
screen` commands to evaluate Journeys. The instructions for device interaction
apply here as well.

A journey is an XML-specified test of an Android app's behavior. It consists of a list of `<action>` elements. For example:
`xml
<journey name="My Journey">
<description>
A sample journey to illustrate the format
</description>
<actions>
<action>
Tap the "Home" icon
</action>
<action>
Verify that the app is on its Home screen
</action>
</actions>
</journey>`

Evaluate a journey by proceeding through the `<actions>` list in sequential order. Evaluate each `<action>` block individually.
A journey succeeds if all elements in the `<actions>` list succeed.

A journey is a test case for an app. The journey XML is the source of truth; if the app disagrees with the journey, the app has failed.
Additionally, if the app exits, crashes, or freezes, journey evaluation stops and the journey fails.

**IMPORTANT** - Execute each step EXACTLY as written, and independently of other steps! If an action says to `"tap the first search result"`,
you MUST find the search results and tap the first one. Do this even if you believe you know the intent behind the action.

### Taking Actions

Some `<action>` elements specify UI interactions to perform on the running Android app. Perform the interaction and verify that the app does
not crash or behave in an unexpected manner. This is the *only* verification you should perform for an `<action>`.

If the interaction cannot be performed as specified, the journey fails.
Example:
`<action>Click the red button</action>`
If you determine a red button is not present in the UI, the journey fails.

If the text of an `<action>` specifies a list of actions, break it into sub-actions and evaluate them individually:
Example:
`<action>Search for soda and add the first result to the cart</action>`
This should be evaluated as:
`<action>Search for soda</action>
<action>Add the first result to the cart</action>`

If an `<action>` contains something that is not a specification for a UI interaction, alert the user that the journey is malformed and exit
early, specifying the error in question.

### Verifying Expectations

`<action>` elements that begin with "check" or "verify" specify expectations for the current state of the Android app. Determine the current
state of the app and check if the expectations are met.

Determine the current state of the app by inspecting the current screen of the device without interacting with it.
Example:
`<action>Check if "Switch 2" is visible on the screen</action>`
This requires only inspecting the current screen, not scrolling or interacting. If "Switch 2" is not currently visible, the action fails.

If the expectations are not met, mark the `<action>` as a failure and the journey evaluation ends. A single `<action>` may contain
multiple expectations.
Example:
`<action>Verify that the app is on the Home screen, the Home icon is blue, and the temperature is displayed</action>`
This `<action>` fails if ANY of the following are false:
- The app is on the Home screen
- There is a Home icon, and it is blue
- A temperature is displayed

### Handling failure

When running a journey, evaluate it as a test. Failure is acceptable, and often expected. Proper reporting of failures is the priority.

Keep debugging and troubleshooting to a minimum; assume that tools are showing you the correct output every time. The goal is to determine
if the *current* Android app can correctly handle the *current* steps outlined in the journey. Suggestions for bug fixes, clarification, or
other improvements should be kept to journey evaluation summary at the end.

### Summarizing

After evaluating the whole journey, output a markdown (.md) file describing the results.

The file should have the following format:

```markdown
# Journey: <Name of the journey>

## Results

  <!-- Append "✅" to the action header if the instruction was evaluated or "❌" if the instruction could not be evaluated -->
### Action: Click the blue button ✅
- **Commands**:
  <!-- A list of the ADB commands executed while evaluating the instruction -->
  - `adb shell input swipe 490 200 500 500 500`
  - `adb shell input tap 45 920`

  <!-- Failure reasons, feedback, or other useful information -->
- **Comment**: The journey step doesn't specify that the button requires scrolling to see

### Action: Check if "Switch 2" is visible on the screen ✅
- **Screenshot**: [switch_2_screenshot.png](path/to/screenshot)
- **Comment**: Confirmed both in layout and visually

### Action: The home screen is shown ❌
- **Comment**: The settings page was shown

<!-- Append nothing to the action header if the action was not evaluated because the journey execution ended early -->
### Action: Swipe down to view active notifications
```

## Doc searching

The `docs` command searches authoritative, high-quality Android developer
documentation in the Android Knowledge Base. By providing a few keywords, this
tool will return high quality articles that contain examples or guidance on how
to use Android APIs or libraries. Use this tool to obtain additional information
on how to achieve Android-specific tasks or to know more about Android APIs,
surfaces, libraries, or devices.

Always use this tool to get the most up-to-date information about Android
concepts. Typical good use cases are:
- Finding migration guides for APIs.
- Finding examples for APIs.
- Finding up-to-date information about Android APIs.
- Finding best practices for Android concepts.

## Running APKs

Use the `run` command to run Android apps.

## Managing emulators

Manage Android Virtual Devices (AVDs) using the `android emulator` command

## Managing skills

Manage agent skills for Android using the `android skills` command.

## Updating the CLI

Update the Android CLI using the `android update` command.

- elements with non-empty `interactions` or `state`
To return all elements, use the `--full` flag

If `layout` continues to fail, use `android screen capture --annotate` to inspect the app.

### Screenshot

`android screen capture -o <file path>` (or `--output=<file path>`) saves a PNG of the current device screen to `<file path>`.

Use `screen capture` as a secondary means of examining an Android app
Examples:
- Understanding the content of an on-screen image
- Looking at a `WebView` (web content does not always appear in the ui dump)
- Trying to find a UI element by its visual appearance

**IMPORTANT** : Always *VISUALLY* examine the PNG image returned from any `android screen` command BEFORE doing anything else.

#### Annotated Screenshot

`android screen capture --annotate -o <file path>` (or `-a -o <file path>`)
`android screen resolve --screenshot <path> --string <string>`

The `--annotate` command adds numerical labels and bounding boxes around UI elements. Use this command to locate UI elements that cannot
be located in the `layout` output.

To refer to these labels in input commands, use `screen resolve` to convert labels into coordinates:

`android screen resolve --screenshot <file path> --string "#3"` returns `<x coord of region 3> <y coord of region 3>`

To save turns, you can combine shell commands:

`adb shell input $(android screen resolve --screenshot screen.png --string "tap #34")`

This command taps on region #34 from `screen.png`

### Input

Use `adb shell input` for interacting with Android devices.
Refer to the `"interactions"` property of an element for what interactions can be performed on a particular element.

Interact with UI elements with their `center` coordinate or their `bounds` coordinates:
`json
{
"key": -248568265,
"class": "android.widget.Button",
"bounds": "[138,9][167,38]",
"center": "[152,23]"
}`
To tap on this button, you would execute `adb shell input tap 152 23`. This taps the center.

```json
{
  "key": 12487234,
  "class": "com.example.ui.ScrollableList",
  "bounds": "[100,200][400,600]",
  "center": "[250,400]"
}
```

To scroll down on this list, you would execute `adb shell input swipe 250 400 250 200 500`. This swipes from the center to the top over 500ms.

#### Text Input

To enter text, ensure the field is focused and execute `adb shell input text "<text>"`.

- **Spaces (`%s`):** Replace spaces with `%s` (Android ignores text after raw spaces): `adb shell input text "Hello%sworld"` (enters `"Hello world"`).
- **Special characters:** Escape shell metacharacters (`&`, `$`, `(`, `)`, `!`): `adb shell input text "AT\&T"` or `adb shell input text 'Price:\$10'`.
- **Submit / Enter:** `adb shell input keyevent 66`

### Android Interaction Rules

1. Always ensure text input fields have `"FOCUSED"` in their `"state"` list before entering text.
2. If an element has `"SCROLLABLE"` in its `"interactions"` list, try scrolling it when looking for missing UI elements.
3. Always scroll slowly when executing scroll inputs. The 5th argument to `adb shell input swipe` controls scroll duration.
4. Content may take time to load; if a `layout` is missing information after you take an action, wait a few seconds, then perform `layout` again to see if anything changes.

## Running journey tests

Journey tests involve device interaction; use the `android layout` and `android
screen` commands to evaluate Journeys. The instructions for device interaction
apply here as well.

A journey is an XML-specified test of an Android app's behavior. It consists of a list of `<action>` elements. For example:
`xml
<journey name="My Journey">
<description>
A sample journey to illustrate the format
</description>
<actions>
<action>
Tap the "Home" icon
</action>
<action>
Verify that the app is on its Home screen
</action>
</actions>
</journey>`

Evaluate a journey by proceeding through the `<actions>` list in sequential order. Evaluate each `<action>` block individually.
A journey succeeds if all elements in the `<actions>` list succeed.

A journey is a test case for an app. The journey XML is the source of truth; if the app disagrees with the journey, the app has failed.
Additionally, if the app exits, crashes, or freezes, journey evaluation stops and the journey fails.

**IMPORTANT** - Execute each step EXACTLY as written, and independently of other steps! If an action says to `"tap the first search result"`,
you MUST find the search results and tap the first one. Do this even if you believe you know the intent behind the action.

### Taking Actions

Some `<action>` elements specify UI interactions to perform on the running Android app. Perform the interaction and verify that the app does
not crash or behave in an unexpected manner. This is the *only* verification you should perform for an `<action>`.

If the interaction cannot be performed as specified, the journey fails.
Example:
`<action>Click the red button</action>`
If you determine a red button is not present in the UI, the journey fails.

If the text of an `<action>` specifies a list of actions, break it into sub-actions and evaluate them individually:
Example:
`<action>Search for soda and add the first result to the cart</action>`
This should be evaluated as:
`<action>Search for soda</action>
<action>Add the first result to the cart</action>`

If an `<action>` contains something that is not a specification for a UI interaction, alert the user that the journey is malformed and exit
early, specifying the error in question.

### Verifying Expectations

`<action>` elements that begin with "check" or "verify" specify expectations for the current state of the Android app. Determine the current
state of the app and check if the expectations are met.

Determine the current state of the app by inspecting the current screen of the device without interacting with it.
Example:
`<action>Check if "Switch 2" is visible on the screen</action>`
This requires only inspecting the current screen, not scrolling or interacting. If "Switch 2" is not currently visible, the action fails.

If the expectations are not met, mark the `<action>` as a failure and the journey evaluation ends. A single `<action>` may contain
multiple expectations.
Example:
`<action>Verify that the app is on the Home screen, the Home icon is blue, and the temperature is displayed</action>`
This `<action>` fails if ANY of the following are false:
- The app is on the Home screen
- There is a Home icon, and it is blue
- A temperature is displayed

### Handling failure

When running a journey, evaluate it as a test. Failure is acceptable, and often expected. Proper reporting of failures is the priority.

Keep debugging and troubleshooting to a minimum; assume that tools are showing you the correct output every time. The goal is to determine
if the *current* Android app can correctly handle the *current* steps outlined in the journey. Suggestions for bug fixes, clarification, or
other improvements should be kept to journey evaluation summary at the end.

### Summarizing

After evaluating the whole journey, output a markdown (.md) file describing the results.

The file should have the following format:

```markdown
# Journey: <Name of the journey>

## Results

  <!-- Append "✅" to the action header if the instruction was evaluated or "❌" if the instruction could not be evaluated -->
### Action: Click the blue button ✅
- **Commands**:
  <!-- A list of the ADB commands executed while evaluating the instruction -->
  - `adb shell input swipe 490 200 500 500 500`
  - `adb shell input tap 45 920`

  <!-- Failure reasons, feedback, or other useful information -->
- **Comment**: The journey step doesn't specify that the button requires scrolling to see

### Action: Check if "Switch 2" is visible on the screen ✅
- **Screenshot**: [switch_2_screenshot.png](path/to/screenshot)
- **Comment**: Confirmed both in layout and visually

### Action: The home screen is shown ❌
- **Comment**: The settings page was shown

<!-- Append nothing to the action header if the action was not evaluated because the journey execution ended early -->
### Action: Swipe down to view active notifications
```

skills.body:
---
name: credential-holder
description: Implement digital credential holder (wallet) registration, presentation,
  and issuance handling in an Android app using the Jetpack Credential Manager Registry
  API. Use this skill when building a digital wallet or holder app in an Android project,
  registering SD-JWT or mdoc credential metadata with RegistryManager and OpenId4VpRegistry,
  configuring inline issuance entries, registering OpenID4VCI creation options with
  RegisterCreationOptionsRequest, or handling GET_CREDENTIAL and CREATE_CREDENTIAL
  intents with PendingIntentHandler. Don't use for requesting credentials as a verifier,
  issuing credentials from an issuer app, passkeys, or carrier TS.43 phone number
  verification.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
metadata:
  author: Google LLC
  last-updated: '2026-11-20'
  keywords:
  - Android
  - identity
  - digital credentials
  - Credential Manager
  - credential holder
  - wallet app
  - RegistryManager
  - OpenId4VpRegistry
  - PendingIntentHandler
  - RegisterCreationOptionsRequest
  - mdoc
  - SD-JWT
  - OpenID4VP
  - OpenID4VCI
---

Build an Android digital wallet (holder) app that registers credential metadata
(`SdJwtEntry` and `MdocEntry`) with Credential Manager using `RegistryManager`
and `OpenId4VpRegistry`, registers OpenID4VCI creation options with
`RegisterCreationOptionsRequest`, and handles incoming `GET_CREDENTIAL`
presentation and `CREATE_CREDENTIAL` issuance requests with
`PendingIntentHandler`. When reviewing holder credential storage concepts,
presentation flows, or issuance handling, consult
[About storing digital credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/about-storing-digital-credentials.md), [Present credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/present-credentials.md), and
[Handle credential issuance](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/handle-credential-issuance.md). When requesting credentials as a relying
party, suggest the `credential-verifier` skill; when provisioning credentials
from an issuer app, suggest the `credential-issuer` skill.

## Prerequisites and setup

- **Android version compatibility:** The Holder API is supported on Android 6 (API level 23) and higher.
- **Build config permission:** Ask for user confirmation before modifying `settings.gradle.kts`, root `build.gradle.kts`, or `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, unless already requested by the user or running non-interactively.
- **Dependencies and package mapping:** Add the Credential Manager and Registry artifacts to the app module build script (`app/build.gradle.kts` or `app/build.gradle`; when checking full dependency declarations, consult [Present credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/present-credentials.md) and [Handle credential issuance](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/handle-credential-issuance.md)):

| Artifact | Key classes, constructor signatures, and package |
|---|---|
| `androidx.credentials:credentials:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | `GetCredentialResponse`, `GetDigitalCredentialOption`, `DigitalCredential(credentialJson: String)`, `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest`, `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse(responseJson: String)`, and `ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi` in `androidx.credentials`; `PendingIntentHandler`, `CallingAppInfo`, `ProviderGetCredentialRequest`, and `ProviderCreateCredentialRequest` in `androidx.credentials.provider`; `GetCredentialException` and `CreateCredentialException` subtypes in `androidx.credentials.exceptions` |
| `androidx.credentials.registry:registry-digitalcredentials-mdoc:1.0.0-alpha05` | `MdocEntry(docType: String, fields: List<MdocField>, entryDisplayPropertySet: Set<EntryDisplayProperties>, id: String)`, `MdocField(namespace: String, identifier: String, fieldValue: Any?, fieldDisplayPropertySet: Set<FieldDisplayProperties>)`, and `MdocInlineIssuanceEntry` in `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.mdoc` |
| `androidx.credentials.registry:registry-digitalcredentials-openid:1.0.0-alpha05` | `OpenId4VpRegistry(credentialEntries: List<DigitalCredentialEntry>, id: String, intentAction: String = RegistryManager.ACTION_GET_CREDENTIAL, inlineIssuanceEntries: List<InlineIssuanceEntry> = emptyList(), supportedProtocols: List<String> = ...)` in `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.openid4vp` |
| `androidx.credentials.registry:registry-digitalcredentials-sdjwtvc:1.0.0-alpha05` | `SdJwtEntry(verifiableCredentialType: String, claims: List<SdJwtClaim>, entryDisplayPropertySet: Set<EntryDisplayProperties>, id: String)`, `SdJwtClaim(path: List<String>, value: Any?, fieldDisplayPropertySet: Set<FieldDisplayProperties>, isSelectivelyDisclosable: Boolean = true)`, and `SdJwtInlineIssuanceEntry` in `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.sdjwt` |
| `androidx.credentials.registry:registry-provider:1.0.0-alpha05` | `RegistryManager`, `RegisterCreationOptionsRequest(type: String, id: String, creationOptions: ByteArray, matcher: ByteArray, intentAction: String = RegistryManager.ACTION_CREATE_CREDENTIAL)`, `ProviderGetCredentialRequest.selectedCredentialSet`, `ProviderGetCredentialRequest.selectedEntryId`, and `ProviderCreateCredentialRequest.selectedEntryId` in `androidx.credentials.registry.provider`; `DigitalCredentialEntry`, `EntryDisplayProperties`, `FieldDisplayProperties`, `InlineIssuanceEntry`, `InlineIssuanceEntry.InlineIssuanceDisplayProperties`, `VerificationEntryDisplayProperties(title: CharSequence, subtitle: CharSequence?, icon: Bitmap, ...)` (`icon` is non-null `android.graphics.Bitmap`), and `VerificationFieldDisplayProperties(displayName: CharSequence, displayValue: CharSequence?)` in `androidx.credentials.registry.provider.digitalcredentials` |
| `androidx.credentials.registry:registry-provider-play-services:1.0.0-alpha05` | Google Play services provider integration for Credential Manager Registry |

### Expected inputs and file scope

- **Required inputs:** The credential formats stored by the wallet (`SdJwtEntry` or `MdocEntry`), whether the wallet supports presentation (`GET_CREDENTIAL`), issuer-initiated issuance (`CREATE_CREDENTIAL`), or inline issuance, and the privileged browser allowlist JSON for caller verification.
- **Files to modify:** `app/build.gradle.kts`, `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (for exported `GET_CREDENTIAL` and `CREATE_CREDENTIAL` activities), wallet registry managers, presentation and issuance `Activity` classes, and UI screens (such as `MainActivity.kt`).

## Codebase exploration

Before modifying files, inspect the Android project:

1. **Validate baseline build and inspect configuration:** Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to confirm the project compiles before making changes, and check `app/build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, and `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` for existing `androidx.credentials` or `androidx.credentials.registry` dependencies and exported holder activities.
2. **Locate wallet storage and UI entry points:** Identify where credentials are stored and locate the primary `Activity` or Compose screen (such as `MainActivity.kt` or `TasksScreen.kt`) to wire credential registration and wallet UI state.

## Critical implementation mandates

Follow the implementation steps and code snippets in
[About storing digital credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/about-storing-digital-credentials.md), [Present credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/present-credentials.md), and
[Handle credential issuance](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-holder/handle-credential-issuance.md), and apply these non-obvious rules:

- **Opt in to experimental APIs:** Annotate classes or functions referencing `GetDigitalCredentialOption`, `DigitalCredential`, `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest`, or `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **Use exact package names for registry artifacts:**
  - `registry-digitalcredentials-openid` exposes `OpenId4VpRegistry` in package `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.openid4vp` (not `.openid`).
  - `registry-digitalcredentials-sdjwtvc` exposes `SdJwtEntry`, `SdJwtClaim`, and `SdJwtInlineIssuanceEntry` in package `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.sdjwt` (not `.sdjwtvc`).
  - `registry-digitalcredentials-mdoc` exposes `MdocEntry`, `MdocField`, and `MdocInlineIssuanceEntry` in package `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.mdoc`.
  - `registry-provider` exposes `DigitalCredentialEntry`, `EntryDisplayProperties`, `FieldDisplayProperties`, `InlineIssuanceEntry`, `VerificationEntryDisplayProperties`, and `VerificationFieldDisplayProperties` in package `androidx.credentials.registry.provider.digitalcredentials`.
- **Keep registry and entry `id` strings within 64 characters:** The `id` parameter on `SdJwtEntry`, `MdocEntry`, `OpenId4VpRegistry`, and `RegisterCreationOptionsRequest` must be at most 64 characters (longer IDs throw `IllegalArgumentException`), and `VerificationEntryDisplayProperties` requires a non-null `android.graphics.Bitmap` `icon`.
- **Declare exported manifest activities for holder intents:** Declare exported (`android:exported="true"`) presentation and issuance activities in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` with `<intent-filter>` blocks containing category `android.intent.category.DEFAULT` and action `androidx.credentials.registry.provider.action.GET_CREDENTIAL` (for presentation and inline issuance) or `androidx.credentials.registry.provider.action.CREATE_CREDENTIAL` (for issuer-initiated issuance).
- **Handle presentation and issuance intents safely:**
  - In the `GET_CREDENTIAL` activity, inspect `request.selectedCredentialSet` and `request.selectedEntryId` (including checking whether the selected ID matches a registered `MdocInlineIssuanceEntry` or `SdJwtInlineIssuanceEntry`), verify caller origin using `request.callingAppInfo.getOrigin(privilegedAppsJson)` for browsers or `"android:apk-key-hash:$certHash"` (with a null or empty check on `signingCertificateHistory`) for Android apps, and initialize `val resultData = Intent()` before calling `PendingIntentHandler.setGetCredentialResponse(resultData, ...)` or `setGetCredentialException(resultData, ...)`.
  - In the `CREATE_CREDENTIAL` activity (used for issuer-initiated offers using `RegisterCreationOptionsRequest` with the wallet's `creationOptions` bytes and issuance Wasm `matcher` bytes), null-check the nullable result of `PendingIntentHandler.retrieveProviderCreateCredentialRequest(intent)` before reading `callingRequest` and `selectedEntryId`. Once a newly issued credential is stored, re-register the wallet's updated credential list with `OpenId4VpRegistry` (`registryManager.registerCredentials`) under the same registry `id` so the credential can be presented.
- **Strip the leading sign byte from `BigInteger.toByteArray()` in JWK
  coordinates:** `BigInteger.toByteArray()` returns a two's-complement signed array that prepends a leading `0x00` sign byte when the most significant bit is set (producing 33 bytes instead of 32 bytes for P-256). Strip any leading `0x00` sign byte before Base64url-encoding JWK `x` and `y` coordinates so issuer key attestation verification doesn't fail.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Experimental API compilation error | `GetDigitalCredentialOption`, `DigitalCredential`, `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest`, and `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` require opt-in | Add `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` to the calling class or function. |
| Unresolved reference `OpenId4VpRegistry` or `SdJwtEntry` | Importing `.openid` or `.sdjwtvc` instead of the actual package names | Import `OpenId4VpRegistry` from `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.openid4vp` and `SdJwtEntry` from `androidx.credentials.registry.digitalcredentials.sdjwt`. |
| Holder app does not appear in Credential Manager selector | Metadata not registered or `GET_CREDENTIAL` / `CREATE_CREDENTIAL` activity missing from `AndroidManifest.xml` | Call `registryManager.registerCredentials` or `registerCreationOptions` and declare exported activities with the `androidx.credentials.registry.provider.action.*` intent filters. |

skills.body:
---
name: credential-issuer
description: Issue digital credentials to user holder wallets from an Android issuer
  app over OpenID4VCI using Jetpack Credential Manager and hardware-backed Android
  Keystore attestation. Use this skill when building an Android credential issuer
  app, provisioning credentials to wallets with CreateDigitalCredentialRequest and
  CredentialManager.createCredential, constructing OpenID4VCI (openid4vci-v1) credential
  offer JSON payloads, or configuring and validating android_keystore_attestation
  certificate chains and c_nonce challenges. Don't use for holder wallet registration
  (RegistryManager), requesting credentials as a verifier (GetDigitalCredentialOption),
  passkeys, or carrier TS.43 phone number verification.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
metadata:
  author: Google LLC
  last-updated: '2026-11-20'
  keywords:
  - Android
  - identity
  - digital credentials
  - Credential Manager
  - credential issuer
  - CreateDigitalCredentialRequest
  - CreateDigitalCredentialResponse
  - OpenID4VCI
  - openid4vci-v1
  - Keystore attestation
  - android_keystore_attestation
  - c_nonce
  - attestationChallenge
---

Build an Android credential issuer app that provisions digital credentials into
a user's holder wallet over OpenID4VCI (`openid4vci-v1`) using
`CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` and `credentialManager.createCredential()`,
alongside backend hardware-backed Android Keystore attestation
(`android_keystore_attestation`). When reviewing digital credential
architecture, client issuance flows, or Keystore attestation requirements,
consult [Digital credentials overview](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/index.md), [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md), and
[Hardware-backed attestation](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/keystore-attestation.md). When building a holder wallet app that
receives and stores issued credentials, suggest the `credential-holder` skill;
when requesting credentials as a verifier, suggest the `credential-verifier`
skill.

## Prerequisites and setup

- **Android version compatibility:** Supported with `androidx.credentials:credentials` `1.6.0` and higher (`minSdk` 23 or higher).
- **Build config permission:** Ask for user confirmation before modifying `settings.gradle.kts`, root `build.gradle.kts`, or `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, unless already requested by the user or running non-interactively.
- **Dependencies and package mapping:** Add the Credential Manager artifacts to the app module build script (`app/build.gradle.kts` or `app/build.gradle`; when checking full dependency declarations, consult [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md)):

| Artifact | Key classes, constructor signatures, and package |
|---|---|
| `androidx.credentials:credentials:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | `CredentialManager`, `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest(requestJson: String, origin: String?)`, `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse(responseJson: String)`, and `ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi` in `androidx.credentials`; `CreateCredentialException`, `CreateCredentialCancellationException`, `CreateCredentialInterruptedException`, `CreateCredentialNoCreateOptionException`, `CreateCredentialUnsupportedException`, `CreateCredentialProviderConfigurationException`, `CreateCredentialCustomException`, and `CreateCredentialUnknownException` in `androidx.credentials.exceptions` |
| `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | Google Play services provider integration for Credential Manager |

### Expected inputs and file scope

- **Required inputs:** The `credential_issuer` URL, `credential_configuration_ids`, and grant type (`pre-authorized_code` with optional `tx_code` or `authorization_code` with `issuer_state`).
- **Files to modify:** `app/build.gradle.kts`, issuer client or repository classes, ViewModels, and UI screens (such as `MainActivity.kt`).

## Codebase exploration

Before modifying files, inspect the Android project:

1. **Validate baseline build and inspect configuration:** Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to confirm the project compiles before making changes, and check `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml` for `minSdk` and `androidx.credentials` dependencies.
2. **Locate target UI entry points:** Identify the `Activity` or Compose screen (such as `MainActivity.kt` or `TasksScreen.kt`) where credential issuance is triggered so `credentialManager.createCredential()` receives an `Activity` `Context`.

## Critical implementation mandates

Follow the step-by-step client implementation in [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md) and
apply these non-obvious rules:

- **Opt in to experimental APIs:** Annotate classes or functions referencing `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` or `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **Enclose the OpenID4VCI request JSON in root `{ ... }` braces:** The example JSON snippet in [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md) starts directly with `"requests":
  [...]` without outer braces. Always wrap the root payload in `{ "requests":
  [...] }` with `"protocol": "openid4vci-v1"` (not `"openid4vci1.0"`) and a `"data"` object specifying `"credential_issuer"`, `"credential_configuration_ids"` (a JSON array of one or more credential configuration IDs), and `"grants"` (such as `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code` or `authorization_code`).
- **Pass `origin = null` in standard Android issuer apps:** When instantiating `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest(requestJson = issuanceRequestJson, origin =
  null)`, always pass `origin = null` for standard Android issuer apps. Only privileged browsers holding `android.permission.CREDENTIAL_MANAGER_SET_ORIGIN` pass a non-null `origin`; passing a non-null `origin` from a standard app throws a `SecurityException`.
- **Handle asynchronous issuance completion and exceptions:** Cast the returned `CreateCredentialResponse` from `credentialManager.createCredential()` to `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` and inspect `response.responseJson` (noting that actual credential provisioning can complete asynchronously after the holder accepts the offer), and catch all `CreateCredentialException` subtypes shown in [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md).

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Experimental API compilation error | `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` and `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` require opt-in | Add `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` to the calling class or function. |
| `SecurityException` on `createCredential` | Non-null `origin` passed by a non-privileged Android app | Pass `origin = null` to `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest`. |
| `CreateCredentialNoCreateOptionException` thrown | No installed wallet app has registered matching `openid4vci-v1` creation options | Verify the JSON is wrapped in `{ "requests": [...] }` with `"protocol": "openid4vci-v1"` and prompt the user to install or set up a compatible digital wallet app. |
| Keystore attestation generation fails on holder device | `c_nonce` exceeds 128 UTF-8 bytes | Restrict `c_nonce` generation on the issuer's nonce endpoint to at most 128 UTF-8 bytes. |

## Verification and reporting guidelines

- \[ \] Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to verify the Android project compiles without errors.
- \[ \] Verify `app/build.gradle.kts` includes `androidx.credentials:credentials` and `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth`.
- \[ \] Verify `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` passes `origin = null` and uses a valid `{ "requests": [...] }` JSON object with `"protocol": "openid4vci-v1"`.
- \[ \] Verify `credentialManager.createCredential()` is called with an `Activity` `Context` and catches `CreateCredentialException` subtypes.

### Post-implementation warnings for the human developer

Present these backend reminders from [Hardware-backed attestation](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/keystore-attestation.md) after
completing client-side issuer code changes:

1. **Issuer `.well-known` attestation metadata:** In the issuer backend's `credential_configurations_supported` metadata, declare `proof_types_supported.android_keystore_attestation` with `proof_signing_alg_values_supported` (such as `["ES256"]`) and `key_attestations_required` (`key_mint_security_level` in `["Software",
   "TrustedEnvironment", "StrongBox"]` and `user_auth_types` in `["LSKF",
   "BIOMETRIC"]`).
2. **Nonce size limit (128 bytes max):** Verify `c_nonce` values generated by the issuer's nonce endpoint are at most 128 UTF-8 bytes so they fit in the Android Keystore `attestationChallenge` `OCTET_STRING`.
3. **Backend X.509 attestation chain validation:** Validate each Base64-encoded X.509 certificate chain in `proofs.android_keystore_attestation` on the issuer's backend server (for example, using the server-side Android Key Attestation library): verify the chain back to the Google hardware Root of Trust, check the certificate revocation status list, verify the `attestationChallenge` in the leaf certificate matches `c_nonce`, and check `keyMintSecurityLevel` and `userAuthType` against the issuer's metadata requirements before signing credentials.

## Antipatterns

- **NEVER** implement digital credential issuance using only generic Android share intents (`Intent.ACTION_SEND`) or local storage without integrating `CredentialManager` and `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest`.
- **NEVER** pass a non-null `origin` to `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` from a standard Android issuer app; always pass `origin = null`.
- **NEVER** generate a `c_nonce` longer than 128 UTF-8 bytes for Android Keystore attestation.

## Best practices

- **MUST** annotate classes or functions using `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` and `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **MUST** handle `CreateCredentialException` subtypes (including `CreateCredentialCancellationException`, `CreateCredentialNoCreateOptionException`, and `CreateCredentialUnsupportedException`) when calling `credentialManager.createCredential()`.
- **MUST** verify the `attestationChallenge` in the leaf certificate extension matches `c_nonce` and check Android Keystore certificate revocation during backend key attestation validation.

2. **Locate target UI entry points:** Identify the `Activity` or Compose screen (such as `MainActivity.kt` or `TasksScreen.kt`) where credential issuance is triggered so `credentialManager.createCredential()` receives an `Activity` `Context`.

## Critical implementation mandates

Follow the step-by-step client implementation in [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md) and
apply these non-obvious rules:

- **Opt in to experimental APIs:** Annotate classes or functions referencing `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` or `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **Enclose the OpenID4VCI request JSON in root `{ ... }` braces:** The example JSON snippet in [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md) starts directly with `"requests":
  [...]` without outer braces. Always wrap the root payload in `{ "requests":
  [...] }` with `"protocol": "openid4vci-v1"` (not `"openid4vci1.0"`) and a `"data"` object specifying `"credential_issuer"`, `"credential_configuration_ids"` (a JSON array of one or more credential configuration IDs), and `"grants"` (such as `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:pre-authorized_code` or `authorization_code`).
- **Pass `origin = null` in standard Android issuer apps:** When instantiating `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest(requestJson = issuanceRequestJson, origin =

- **Handle asynchronous issuance completion and exceptions:** Cast the returned `CreateCredentialResponse` from `credentialManager.createCredential()` to `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` and inspect `response.responseJson` (noting that actual credential provisioning can complete asynchronously after the holder accepts the offer), and catch all `CreateCredentialException` subtypes shown in [Issue credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-issuer/issue-credentials.md).

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Experimental API compilation error | `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` and `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` require opt-in | Add `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` to the calling class or function. |

- \[ \] Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to verify the Android project compiles without errors.
- \[ \] Verify `app/build.gradle.kts` includes `androidx.credentials:credentials` and `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth`.
- \[ \] Verify `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` passes `origin = null` and uses a valid `{ "requests": [...] }` JSON object with `"protocol": "openid4vci-v1"`.
- \[ \] Verify `credentialManager.createCredential()` is called with an `Activity` `Context` and catches `CreateCredentialException` subtypes.

### Post-implementation warnings for the human developer

completing client-side issuer code changes:

1. **Issuer `.well-known` attestation metadata:** In the issuer backend's `credential_configurations_supported` metadata, declare `proof_types_supported.android_keystore_attestation` with `proof_signing_alg_values_supported` (such as `["ES256"]`) and `key_attestations_required` (`key_mint_security_level` in `["Software",
   "TrustedEnvironment", "StrongBox"]` and `user_auth_types` in `["LSKF",
   "BIOMETRIC"]`).
2. **Nonce size limit (128 bytes max):** Verify `c_nonce` values generated by the issuer's nonce endpoint are at most 128 UTF-8 bytes so they fit in the Android Keystore `attestationChallenge` `OCTET_STRING`.
3. **Backend X.509 attestation chain validation:** Validate each Base64-encoded X.509 certificate chain in `proofs.android_keystore_attestation` on the issuer's backend server (for example, using the server-side Android Key Attestation library): verify the chain back to the Google hardware Root of Trust, check the certificate revocation status list, verify the `attestationChallenge` in the leaf certificate matches `c_nonce`, and check `keyMintSecurityLevel` and `userAuthType` against the issuer's metadata requirements before signing credentials.

## Antipatterns

- **NEVER** implement digital credential issuance using only generic Android share intents (`Intent.ACTION_SEND`) or local storage without integrating `CredentialManager` and `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest`.
- **NEVER** pass a non-null `origin` to `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` from a standard Android issuer app; always pass `origin = null`.
- **NEVER** generate a `c_nonce` longer than 128 UTF-8 bytes for Android Keystore attestation.

## Best practices

- **MUST** annotate classes or functions using `CreateDigitalCredentialRequest` and `CreateDigitalCredentialResponse` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **MUST** handle `CreateCredentialException` subtypes (including `CreateCredentialCancellationException`, `CreateCredentialNoCreateOptionException`, and `CreateCredentialUnsupportedException`) when calling `credentialManager.createCredential()`.
- **MUST** verify the `attestationChallenge` in the leaf certificate extension matches `c_nonce` and check Android Keystore certificate revocation during backend key attestation validation.

---
name: credential-verifier
description: Request and verify digital credentials (such as ISO mdoc mobile driver's
  licenses and SD-JWT credentials) from a holder wallet in an Android app or WebView
  using Jetpack Credential Manager. Use this skill when building a digital credential
  verifier app in an Android project, constructing OpenID4VP (openid4vp-v1-unsigned)
  and Digital Credential Query Language (dcql_query) requests, calling CredentialManager.getCredential
  with GetDigitalCredentialOption, requesting multiple credentials simultaneously,
  or bridging WebView navigator.credentials.get requests with WebViewCompat.WebMessageListener.
  Don't use for holder wallet registration, issuing credentials over OpenID4VCI, passkeys,
  or carrier TS.43 phone number verification.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
metadata:
  author: Google LLC
  last-updated: '2026-11-20'
  keywords:
  - Android
  - identity
  - digital credentials
  - Credential Manager
  - credential verifier
  - GetDigitalCredentialOption
  - DigitalCredential
  - OpenID4VP
  - openid4vp-v1-unsigned
  - DCQL
  - dcql_query
  - mso_mdoc
  - dc+sd-jwt
  - WebView
  - WebMessageListener
---

Build an Android verifier (relying party) app that requests and verifies digital
credentials (`mso_mdoc` and `dc+sd-jwt`) from a user's holder wallet over
OpenID4VP (`openid4vp-v1-unsigned`) and Digital Credential Query Language
(`dcql_query`) using `GetDigitalCredentialOption` and
`credentialManager.getCredential()`, either directly in an Android app or
through a `WebView` JavaScript bridge. When reviewing digital credential
architecture, trust requirements, or verifier implementation snippets, consult
[Digital credentials overview](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/index.md), [About trust and safety](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/trust-safety.md),
[Request credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/request-credential.md), and [Request a credential through WebView](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/webview-request.md). When
building a wallet app that stores and presents credentials, suggest the
`credential-holder` skill; when issuing credentials to a wallet, suggest the
`credential-issuer` skill; when implementing carrier TS.43 phone number
verification, suggest the `phone-number-verification` skill.

## Prerequisites and setup

- **Android version compatibility:** Runtime support for the Verifier API requires Android 9 (API level 28) and higher (`WebView` JavaScript bridge targets API level 23 or higher, and `androidx.credentials` compiles with `minSdk` 23 or higher).
- **Build config permission:** Ask for user confirmation before modifying `settings.gradle.kts`, root `build.gradle.kts`, or `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, unless already requested by the user or running non-interactively.
- **Dependencies and package mapping:** Add the Credential Manager artifacts (and `androidx.webkit` when bridging `WebView` requests) to the app module build script (`app/build.gradle.kts` or `app/build.gradle`; when checking full dependency snippets, consult [Request credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/request-credential.md) and [Request a credential through WebView](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/webview-request.md)):

| Scenario | Artifact | Key classes, constructor signatures, and package |
|---|---|---|
| All verifier flows | `androidx.credentials:credentials:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | `CredentialManager`, `GetCredentialRequest`, `GetCredentialResponse`, `GetDigitalCredentialOption(requestJson: String)`, `DigitalCredential`, and `ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi` in `androidx.credentials`; `GetCredentialException`, `GetCredentialCancellationException`, `GetCredentialInterruptedException`, `NoCredentialException`, `GetCredentialUnknownException`, and `GetCredentialCustomException` in `androidx.credentials.exceptions` |
| All verifier flows | `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | Google Play services provider integration for Credential Manager |
| `WebView` bridge | `androidx.webkit:webkit:1.18.0` | `WebViewCompat`, `WebViewCompat.WebMessageListener`, `WebMessageCompat`, `WebViewFeature`, and `JavaScriptReplyProxy` in `androidx.webkit` |

### Expected inputs and file scope

- **Required inputs:** The credential formats (`mso_mdoc` with `doctype_value` or `dc+sd-jwt` with `vct_values`) and minimum selective-disclosure claims to request, and whether verification runs directly in an Android screen or inside a `WebView`.
- **Files to modify:** `app/build.gradle.kts`, verifier client or repository classes, `WebViewCompat.WebMessageListener` bridge classes (when using `WebView`), ViewModels, and UI screens (such as `MainActivity.kt`).

## Codebase exploration

Before modifying files, inspect the Android project:

1. **Validate baseline build and inspect configuration:** Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to confirm the project compiles before making changes, and check `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml` for `minSdk`, `androidx.credentials`, and `androidx.webkit` dependencies.
2. **Locate target UI entry points:** Identify the `Activity` or Compose screen (such as `MainActivity.kt` or `TasksScreen.kt`) where verification is triggered so `credentialManager.getCredential()` receives an `Activity` `Context`.

## Critical implementation mandates

- **Opt in to experimental APIs:** Annotate classes or functions referencing `GetDigitalCredentialOption` or `DigitalCredential` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` (omitted from the snippet in [Request credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/request-credential.md)).
- **Use the exact OpenID4VP and DCQL JSON schema:** Follow the single-credential (`mso_mdoc` or `dc+sd-jwt`) and multi-credential (`dcql_query.credentials`) JSON schemas in [Request credentials](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/request-credential.md) (`"protocol":
  "openid4vp-v1-unsigned"`, `"response_type": "vp_token"`, `"response_mode": "dc_api"`, `"nonce"`, and `"dcql_query"`). Never wrap the Android `GetDigitalCredentialOption(requestJson)` payload in a browser-only `{"providers": [...]}` object.
- **Send `credentialJson` to the app's backend for verification:** Extract `credential.credentialJson` from `DigitalCredential` and send it with the session `nonce` to the app's backend to verify the cryptographic signature and issuer trust chain; never trust unverified claims directly on the client.
- **Complete the `WebView` listener and `AndroidView` setup:** When following [Request a credential through WebView](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/webview-request.md):
  - Add `androidx.webkit:webkit:1.18.0` alongside the Credential Manager dependencies and inject the `bridge.js` script that intercepts `navigator.credentials.get({ digital })`.
  - Implement `WebViewCompat.WebMessageListener.onPostMessage(view: WebView,
    message: WebMessageCompat, sourceOrigin: Uri, isMainFrame: Boolean,
    replyProxy: JavaScriptReplyProxy)` (described in prose only in [Request a credential through WebView](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/webview-request.md)): verify `isMainFrame` is `true` and `sourceOrigin.scheme == "https"`, parse `message.data`, call `credentialManager.getCredential` with `GetDigitalCredentialOption`, and return `credential.credentialJson` (or a JSON error object) through `replyProxy.postMessage(...)`.
  - Inside `WebView(context).apply { ... }` in `AndroidView`, pass `this` (not an undeclared `webView` variable) to `WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener`, pass the declared `handler` variable to `DigitalCredentialWebListener`, and close the `if (WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported(...))` block before calling `loadUrl("https://...")`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Experimental API compilation error | `GetDigitalCredentialOption` and `DigitalCredential` require opt-in | Add `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` to the calling class or function. |
| Compilation error on `CreateCredentialUnknownException` in `when (e: GetCredentialException)` | `CreateCredential*Exception` doesn't inherit from `GetCredentialException` | Match `GetCredentialUnknownException` and `GetCredentialCustomException` instead. |
| Credential selector fails or returns invalid request | Using a browser `providers` wrapper object instead of OpenID4VP | Use `"requests"` with `"protocol": "openid4vp-v1-unsigned"`, `"response_type": "vp_token"`, `"response_mode": "dc_api"`, and `"dcql_query"`. |
| `WebView` credential request fails silently | `WebMessageListener` not registered or origin not allowed | Check `WebViewFeature.WEB_MESSAGE_LISTENER` and register `WebViewCompat.addWebMessageListener` with explicit HTTPS `allowedOriginRules` before `loadUrl`. |

## Verification and reporting guidelines

- \[ \] Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to verify the Android project compiles without errors.
- \[ \] Verify `app/build.gradle.kts` includes `androidx.credentials:credentials` and `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth` (plus `androidx.webkit:webkit` for `WebView` flows).
- \[ \] Verify the OpenID4VP request JSON uses `"protocol":
  "openid4vp-v1-unsigned"`, `"response_type": "vp_token"`, `"response_mode": "dc_api"`, and `"dcql_query"`.
- \[ \] Verify `credentialManager.getCredential()` is called with an `Activity` `Context` and catches `GetCredentialException` subtypes.

### Post-implementation warnings for the human developer

Present these reminders after completing verifier code changes:

1. **Server-side cryptographic verification:** Generate single-use cryptographic `nonce` values on the app's backend and verify the returned `DigitalCredential.credentialJson` (`vp_token` issuer signature, trust chain, device binding, and nonce) on the backend server before trusting any claims.
2. **Minimum selective disclosure:** Request only the minimum attributes needed (such as `age_over_21` rather than full birth date or address) in `dcql_query`.

## Antipatterns

- **NEVER** implement a digital credential verifier using only a simulated QR scanner or local mock UI without integrating `CredentialManager` and `GetDigitalCredentialOption`.
- **NEVER** invent a top-level `{"providers": [...]}` JSON schema for `GetDigitalCredentialOption(requestJson)` in an Android verifier app; always use `"requests"` with `"protocol": "openid4vp-v1-unsigned"` and `"dcql_query"`.
- **NEVER** trust raw claims parsed on the client without validating `credential.credentialJson` and the session `nonce` on the app's backend.

## Best practices

- **MUST** annotate classes or functions using `GetDigitalCredentialOption` and `DigitalCredential` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **MUST** handle `GetCredentialCancellationException`, `GetCredentialInterruptedException`, `NoCredentialException`, `GetCredentialUnknownException`, and `GetCredentialCustomException` when calling `credentialManager.getCredential()`.
- **MUST** verify `isMainFrame` and `https` `sourceOrigin` in `WebView` `WebMessageListener.onPostMessage` before forwarding credential requests to `CredentialManager`.

skills.body:
---
name: phone-number-verification
description: Verify user phone numbers without SMS in an Android app using the Credential
  Manager DigitalCredential API, OpenID4VP, and carrier-issued TS.43 tokens. Use this
  skill whenever the user asks to verify phone numbers without SMS, implement carrier-based
  phone number verification in an Android project, perform a TelephonyManager.getSimCarrierId
  carrier precheck, or request a TS.43 Digital Credential using CredentialManager,
  GetDigitalCredentialOption, GetCredentialRequest, DigitalCredential, and dc-authorization+sd-jwt
  DCQL queries. Produces Android client-side carrier precheck and Credential Manager
  TS.43 token request code alongside backend OpenID4VP and DCQL request construction
  and token exchange logic. Don't use for SMS OTP, TelephonyManager.getLine1Number
  reads, digital wallet holder registration, or issuing credentials to wallets.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
metadata:
  author: Google LLC
  last-updated: '2026-11-20'
  keywords:
  - Android
  - identity
  - digital credentials
  - phone number verification
  - DigitalCredential API
  - TS.43 token
  - aggregator
  - OpenID4VP
  - Credential Manager API
  - DCQL
---

Implement phishing-resistant, SMS-free phone number verification in an Android
app using Credential Manager's `DigitalCredential` API to request an encrypted,
carrier-issued `TS.43 token` over OpenID4VP and exchange it with an aggregator
or mobile carrier backend for the verified phone number. When reviewing TS.43
architecture and security standards, consult
[About verifying phone numbers](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/credential-verifier/about-verifying-phone-numbers.md). When implementing client and server code
snippets, consult [Implement phone number verification](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/implement-phone-number-verification.md). When verifying
general `mso_mdoc` or `dc+sd-jwt` wallet credentials, suggest the
`credential-verifier` skill.

## Prerequisites and setup

- **Android version compatibility:** Runtime support for the Phone Number Verification API requires Android 10 (API level 29) or higher (while the `androidx.credentials` library compiles with `minSdk` 23 or higher).
- **Aggregator account:** Requires an account with a mobile carrier or cellular aggregator endpoint that supplies DCQL parameters and exchanges `TS.43` tokens.
- **Manifest permission for carrier precheck:** Declare `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE" />` in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` to query `TelephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()` before invoking Credential Manager.
- **Build config permission:** Ask for user confirmation before modifying `settings.gradle.kts`, root `build.gradle.kts`, or `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, unless already requested by the user or running non-interactively.
- **Dependencies and package mapping:** Add the Credential Manager artifacts to the app module build script (`app/build.gradle.kts` or `app/build.gradle`; when checking the latest version declarations, consult [Implement phone number verification](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/implement-phone-number-verification.md)):

| Artifact | Key classes, constructor signatures, and package |
|---|---|
| `androidx.credentials:credentials:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | `CredentialManager`, `GetCredentialRequest`, `GetCredentialResponse`, `GetDigitalCredentialOption(requestJson: String)`, `DigitalCredential`, and `ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi` in `androidx.credentials`; `GetCredentialException`, `GetCredentialCancellationException`, `GetCredentialInterruptedException`, `GetCredentialUnsupportedException`, and `NoCredentialException` in `androidx.credentials.exceptions` |
| `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth:1.7.0-alpha03` (or `1.6.0`+) | Play services provider integration for Credential Manager |

### Expected inputs and file scope

- **Required inputs:** Whether the app is retrieving the device phone number (`number-verification/device-phone-number/ts43`) or verifying an existing user-entered phone number (`number-verification/verify/ts43`), whether dual SIM (`subscription_hint`) or biometric/screen-lock verification (`user_verification_hint`) is needed, and the fallback verification flow when the carrier or device is unsupported.
- **Files to modify:** `app/build.gradle.kts`, `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (for `READ_PHONE_STATE`), phone number verification client or repository classes, ViewModels, and UI screens or `Activity` classes (such as `MainActivity.kt`).
- **Forbidden substitutions:** Don't use `TelephonyManager.getLine1Number()`, `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS`, `SmsRetriever`, or SMS OTP APIs as a substitute for the Credential Manager `DigitalCredential` TS.43 verification flow (only use `TelephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()` for the carrier support precheck, and fall back to SMS only when the carrier or device is unsupported).

## Codebase exploration

Search the Android project before modifying files:

1. **Validate baseline build and inspect configuration:** Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to confirm the project compiles before making changes, check `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml` for `minSdk` and `androidx.credentials` dependencies, and check `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` for `READ_PHONE_STATE`.
2. **Locate UI entry points:** Identify the `Activity` or Compose screen (such as `MainActivity.kt` or `TasksScreen.kt`) where phone number verification is triggered so you pass an `Activity` `Context` to `credentialManager.getCredential()`.

## Critical implementation mandates

Follow the end-to-end steps and code snippets in
[Implement phone number verification](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/implement-phone-number-verification.md) and apply these rules:

- **Opt in to experimental APIs:** Annotate classes or functions referencing `GetDigitalCredentialOption` and `DigitalCredential` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` (omitted from the Kotlin snippet in [Implement phone number verification](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/implement-phone-number-verification.md)).
- **Perform the carrier TS.43 precheck and handle unsupported fallbacks:** Declare `READ_PHONE_STATE` in `AndroidManifest.xml`, query `telephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()`, and check whether the user's carrier supports TS.43 with the app's aggregator backend before calling `credentialManager.getCredential()`. If the carrier is unsupported, or if the device runs below Android 10 (API level 29) or throws `GetCredentialUnsupportedException` or `GetCredentialCancellationException`, trigger a fallback verification flow (such as SMS).
- **Configure DCQL parameters and optional hints:** In each `{ ... }` credential entry inside `requests[0].data.dcql_query.credentials` (with `"protocol": "openid4vp-v1-unsigned"`, `"response_type": "vp_token"`, `"response_mode": "dc_api"`, and a `"nonce"` matching the aggregator DCQL request):
  - Set `"format": "dc-authorization+sd-jwt"` and include `meta.credential_authorization_jwt` from the aggregator.
  - Set `meta.vct_values` to `["number-verification/device-phone-number/ts43"]` to retrieve the device phone number, or `["number-verification/verify/ts43"]` (with `{"path":
    ["phone_number_hint"], "values": [...]}` in `claims`) to verify an existing phone number.
  - Include `{"path": ["subscription_hint"], "values": [...]}` in `claims` when targeting a specific SIM subscription slot, and `{"path":
    ["user_verification_hint"]}` when requiring biometric or screen-lock authentication (which returns `"user_verification_hint"` as `"success"`, `"absent"`, or `"error"` in the response payload, or throws `GetCredentialCancellationException` if the user dismisses the prompt).
- **Avoid syntax pitfalls in the reference server snippets:** When referencing the backend examples in [Implement phone number verification](references/android/identity/digital-credentials/implement-phone-number-verification.md), note that the Python `GenerateDCRequest` snippet contains a Kotlin-style `val
  dc_request =` typo, the response JSON example includes `#` comments, and the error JSON example has a trailing comma; strip those invalid tokens when writing JSON or backend code, check `data.error` (`invalid_request` or `server_error`) first, and index the encrypted token from `data.vp_token[<aggregator_id>][0]`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Experimental API compilation error | `GetDigitalCredentialOption` and `DigitalCredential` require `@ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi` | Add `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)` to the calling class or function. |
| Empty result or `GetCredentialCancellationException` | User canceled (including dismissing biometric `user_verification_hint`), feature unavailable, or SIM carrier does not support TS.43 | Run the `TelephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()` precheck before calling `getCredential()` and fall back to an alternate flow when unsupported. |
| `GetCredentialUnsupportedException` thrown | Device or OS version does not support the Phone Number Verification API (requires Android 10, API 29+) | Check `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.Q` and handle `GetCredentialUnsupportedException` with a fallback flow. |
| Response JSON contains `"error": "invalid_request"` | Malformed OpenID4VP or DCQL request JSON or mismatched `nonce` | Verify `protocol` is `openid4vp-v1-unsigned`, `format` is `dc-authorization+sd-jwt`, `credentials` is a JSON array of `{ ... }` objects, and the outer `nonce` matches the aggregator DCQL `nonce`. |

## Verification and reporting guidelines

- \[ \] Run `./gradlew assembleDebug` to verify the project compiles without errors.
- \[ \] Verify `app/build.gradle.kts` includes `androidx.credentials:credentials` and `androidx.credentials:credentials-play-services-auth`.
- \[ \] Verify `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` declares `READ_PHONE_STATE` and the client performs the `TelephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()` carrier precheck with a fallback when unsupported.
- \[ \] Verify the OpenID4VP request uses `"protocol": "openid4vp-v1-unsigned"`, `"format": "dc-authorization+sd-jwt"`, and `"number-verification/device-phone-number/ts43"` or `"number-verification/verify/ts43"`.
- \[ \] Verify `GetDigitalCredentialOption`, `GetCredentialRequest`, `credentialManager.getCredential()`, and `DigitalCredential` are used with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.

### Post-implementation warnings for the human developer

Present these backend reminders after completing client-side changes:

1. **Aggregator DCQL and token exchange:** Configure the app's backend service to verify carrier IDs from `getSimCarrierId()`, request live DCQL parameters (`credential_authorization_jwt`) from one or more carrier aggregators using a matching `nonce`, and exchange the returned `TS.43 Digital Credential` from `data.vp_token[<aggregator_id>][0]` for the verified phone number.
2. **Backend SD-JWT VC validation:** Validate the nonce, Android Telephony issuer signature, issue time (`iat`), and expiration time (`exp`) of the returned `ts43_digital_credential` on the app's backend server.

## Antipatterns

- **NEVER** use `TelephonyManager.getLine1Number()`, `READ_PHONE_NUMBERS`, `SmsRetriever`, or SMS OTP flows as a substitute for Credential Manager's `DigitalCredential` API (`GetDigitalCredentialOption` and `credentialManager.getCredential()`) when implementing digital credential phone number verification.
- **NEVER** skip the `TelephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()` carrier precheck before calling `credentialManager.getCredential()`.
- **NEVER** attempt to decrypt the encrypted `TS.43 Digital Credential` on the Android client; only the associated aggregator decrypts the payload.
- **NEVER** mismatch the `nonce` in the OpenID4VP request `data` object and the `nonce` sent to the aggregator when generating the DCQL credential object.

## Best practices

- **MUST** annotate classes or functions using `GetDigitalCredentialOption` and `DigitalCredential` with `@OptIn(androidx.credentials.ExperimentalDigitalCredentialApi::class)`.
- **MUST** declare `READ_PHONE_STATE` and call `telephonyManager.getSimCarrierId()` to verify carrier TS.43 support before invoking Credential Manager, falling back to an alternate verification flow when unsupported.
- **MUST** check both `GetCredentialException` (`GetCredentialCancellationException` and `GetCredentialUnsupportedException`) and OpenID4VP error JSON payloads (`invalid_request` and `server_error`).
- **MUST** use `number-verification/device-phone-number/ts43` to retrieve a device phone number and `number-verification/verify/ts43` to verify an existing phone number.
