--- name: edge-to-edge description: Use this skill to migrate your Jetpack Compose app to add adaptive edge-to-edge support and troubleshoot common issues. Use this skill to fix UI components (like buttons or lists) that are obscured by or overlapping with the navigation bar or status bar, fix IME insets, and fix system bar legibility. license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt metadata: author: Google LLC last-updated: '2026-08-24' keywords: - android - compose - system bars - edge-to-edge - status bar - navigation bar --- ## Prerequisites - Project **MUST** use Android Jetpack Compose. - Project **MUST** target SDK 35 or later. If the SDK is lower than 35, increase the SDK to 35. ## Step 1: plan 1. Locate and analyze all Activity classes to detect which have existing edge-to-edge support. For every Activity without edge-to-edge, plan to make each Activity edge-to-edge. 2. In each Activity, Locate and analyze all lists and FAB components to detect which have existing edge-to-edge support. For every component without edge-to-edge support, plan to make each of these components edge-to-edge. 3. In each Activity, scan for `TextField`, `OutlinedTextField`, or `BasicTextField`. If found, then you **MUST** verify the IME doesn't hide the input field by following the IME section of this skill. ## Step 2: add edge-to-edge support 1. Add `enableEdgeToEdge` before `setContent` in `onCreate` in each Activity that does not already call `enableEdgeToEdge`. 2. Add `android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"` in the AndroidManifest.xml for all Activities that use a soft keyboard. ## Step 3: apply insets - The app **MUST** apply system insets, or align content to rulers, so critical UI remains tappable. Choose only one method to avoid double padding: 1. **PREFERRED:** When available, use `Scaffold`s and pass `PaddingValues` to the content lambda. ```kotlin Scaffold { innerPadding -> // innerPadding accounts for system bars and any Scaffold components LazyColumn( modifier = Modifier .fillMaxSize() .consumeWindowInsets(innerPadding), contentPadding = innerPadding ) { /* Content */ } } ```
1. **PREFERRED:** When available, use the automatic inset handling or padding modifiers in material components. - Material 3 Components manages safe areas for its own components, including: - `TopAppBar` - `SmallTopAppBar` - `CenterAlignedTopAppBar` - `MediumTopAppBar` - `LargeTopAppBar` - `BottomAppBar` - `ModalDrawerSheet` - `DismissibleDrawerSheet` - `PermanentDrawerSheet` - `ModalBottomSheet` - `NavigationBar` - `NavigationRail` - For Material 2 Components, use the `windowInsets`parameter to apply insets manually for `BottomAppBar`, `TopAppBar` and `BottomNavigation`. **DO NOT** apply padding to the parent container; instead, pass insets directly to the App Bar component. Applying padding to the parent container prevents the App Bar background from drawing into the system bar area. For example, for `TopAppBar`, choose only one of the following options: 1. **PREFERRED:** `TopAppBar(windowInsets = AppBarDefaults.topAppBarWindowInsets)` 2. `TopAppBar(windowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.exclude(WindowInsets.navigationBars))` 3. `TopAppBar(windowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.add(WindowInsets.captionBar))` 2. For components outside a Scaffold, use padding modifiers, such as `Modifier.safeDrawingPadding()` or `Modifier.windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)`. ```kotlin Box( modifier = Modifier .fillMaxSize() .safeDrawingPadding() ) { Button( onClick = {}, modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomCenter) ) { Text("Login") } } ```
3. For deeply nested components with excessive padding, use `WindowInsetsRulers` (e.g. `Modifier.fitInside(WindowInsetsRulers.SafeDrawing.current)`). See the *IME* section for a code sample. 4. When you need an element (e.g. a custom header or decorative scrim) to equal the dimensions of a system bar, use inset size modifiers (e.g. `Modifier.windowInsetsTopHeight(WindowInsets.systemBars)`). See the *Lists* section for a code sample. ## Adaptive Scaffolds - `NavigationSuiteScaffold` manages safe areas for its own components, like the `NavigationRail` or `NavigationBar`. However, the adaptive scaffolds (e.g. `NavigationSuiteScaffold`, `ListDetailPaneScaffold`) don't propagate PaddingValues to their inner contents. You **MUST** apply insets to **individual** screens or components (e.g., list `contentPadding` or FAB padding) as described in *Step 3* . **DO NOT** apply `safeDrawingPadding` or similar modifiers to the `NavigationSuiteScaffold` parent. This clips and prevents an edge-to-edge screen. ## IME - For each Activity with a soft keyboard, check that `android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"` is set in the AndroidManifest.xml. DO NOT use `SOFT_INPUT_ADJUST_RESIZE` because it is deprecated. Then, maintain focus on the input field. Choose one: - 1. **PREFERRED:** Add `Modifier.fitInside(WindowInsetsRulers.Ime.current)` to the content container. This is preferred over `imePadding()` because it reduces jank and extra padding caused by forgetting to consume insets upstream in the hierarchy. - 2. Add `imePadding` to the content container. The padding modifier **MUST** be placed before `Modifier.verticalScroll()`. Do NOT use `Modifier.imePadding()` if the parent already accounts for the IME with `contentWindowInsets` (e.g. `contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.safeDrawing`). Doing so will cause double padding. ### IMEs with Scaffolds code patterns #### RIGHT RIGHT because `contentWindowInsets` contains IME insets, which are passed to the content lambda as `innerPadding`. ```kotlin // RIGHT Scaffold(contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.safeDrawing) { innerPadding -> Column( modifier = Modifier .padding(innerPadding) .consumeWindowInsets(innerPadding) .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()) ) { /* Content */ } } ```
*** ** * ** *** RIGHT because `fitInside` fits the content to the IME insets regardless of `contentWindowInsets`. ```kotlin // RIGHT Scaffold() { innerPadding -> Column( modifier = Modifier .padding(innerPadding) .consumeWindowInsets(innerPadding) .fitInside(WindowInsetsRulers.Ime.current) .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()) ) { /* Content */ } } ```
*** ** * ** *** RIGHT because the default `contentWindowInsets` does not contain IME insets, and `imePadding()` applies IME insets: ```kotlin // RIGHT Scaffold() { innerPadding -> Column( modifier = Modifier .padding(innerPadding) .consumeWindowInsets(innerPadding) .imePadding() .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()) ) { /* Content */ } } ```
#### WRONG WRONG because there will be excess padding when the IME opens. IME insets are applied twice, once with innerPadding, which contains IME insets from the passed `contentWindowInsets` values, and once with `imePadding`: ```kotlin // WRONG Scaffold(contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.safeDrawing) { innerPadding -> Column( modifier = Modifier .padding(innerPadding) .imePadding() .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()) ) { /* Content */ } } ```
*** ** * ** *** WRONG because the IME will cover up the content. Scaffold's default `contentWindowInsets` does NOT contain IME insets. ```kotlin // WRONG Scaffold() { innerPadding -> Column( modifier = Modifier .padding(innerPadding) .verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()) ) { /* Content */ } } ```
### IMEs without Scaffolds code patterns #### RIGHT The following code samples WILL NOT cause excessive padding. ```kotlin // RIGHT Box( // Insets consumed modifier = Modifier.safeDrawingPadding() // or imePadding(), safeContentPadding(), safeGesturesPadding() ) { Column( modifier = Modifier.imePadding() ) { /* Content */ } } ```
*** ** * ** *** ```kotlin // RIGHT Box( // Insets consumed modifier = Modifier.windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing) // or WindowInsets.ime, WindowInsets.safeContent, WindowInsets.safeGestures ) { Column( modifier = Modifier.imePadding() ) { /* Content */ } } ```
*** ** * ** *** ```kotlin // RIGHT Box( // Insets not consumed, but irrelevant due to fitInside modifier = Modifier.padding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing.asPaddingValues()) // or WindowInsets.ime.asPaddingValues(), WindowInsets.safeContent.asPaddingValues(), WindowInsets.safeGestures.asPaddingValues() ) { Column( modifier = Modifier .fillMaxSize() .fitInside(WindowInsetsRulers.Ime.current) ) { /* Content */ } } ```
#### WRONG The following code sample WILL cause excessive padding because IME insets are applied twice: ```kotlin // WRONG Box( // Insets not consumed modifier = Modifier.padding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing.asPaddingValues()) // or WindowInsets.ime.asPaddingValues(), WindowInsets.safeContent.asPaddingValues(), WindowInsets.safeGestures.asPaddingValues() ) { Column( modifier = Modifier.imePadding() ) { /* Content */ } } ```
## Navigation Bar Contrast \& System Bar Icons - If the Activity uses `enableEdgeToEdge` from `WindowCompat`, you **MUST** set `isAppearanceLightNavigationBars` and `isAppearanceLightStatusBars` to the inverse of the device theme for apps that support light and dark theme so the system bar icons are legible. It's recommended to do this in your theme file. DO NOT do this if the Activities use `enableEdgeToEdge` from `ComponentActivity` because it handles the icon colors automatically. ```kotlin // Only use if calling `enableEdgeToEdge` from `WindowCompat`. // Apply to your theme file. @Composable fun MyTheme( darkTheme: Boolean = isSystemInDarkTheme(), content: @Composable () -> Unit ) { val view = LocalView.current if (!view.isInEditMode) { SideEffect { val window = (view.context as? Activity)?.window ?: return@SideEffect val controller = WindowCompat.getInsetsController(window, view) // Dark icons for Light Mode (!darkTheme), Light icons for Dark Mode controller.isAppearanceLightStatusBars = !darkTheme controller.isAppearanceLightNavigationBars = !darkTheme } } MaterialTheme(content = content) } ```
- If any screen uses a `Scaffold` or a `NavigationSuiteScaffold` with a bottom bar (e.g., `BottomAppBar`, `NavigationBar`), set `window.isNavigationBarContrastEnforced = false` in the corresponding Activity for SDK 29+. This prevents the system from adding a translucent background to the navigation bar, verifying your bottom bar colors extend to the bottom of the screen. ## Lists - Apply inset padding (like `Scaffold`'s `innerPadding`) to the `contentPadding` parameter of scrollable components (e.g. `LazyColumn`, `LazyRow`). DO NOT apply it as a `Modifier.padding()` to the list's parent container, as this clips the content and prevents it from scrolling behind the system bars. - Create a translucent composable covering the system bar so that the icons are still legible. ```kotlin class SystemBarProtectionSnippets : ComponentActivity() { override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) { super.onCreate(savedInstanceState) // enableEdgeToEdge sets window.isNavigationBarContrastEnforced = true // which is used to add a translucent scrim to three-button navigation enableEdgeToEdge() setContent { MyTheme { // Main content MyContent() // After drawing main content, draw status bar protection StatusBarProtection() } } } } @Composable private fun StatusBarProtection( color: Color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceContainer, ) { Spacer( modifier = Modifier .fillMaxWidth() .height( with(LocalDensity.current) { (WindowInsets.statusBars.getTop(this) * 1.2f).toDp() } ) .background( brush = Brush.verticalGradient( colors = listOf( color.copy(alpha = 1f), color.copy(alpha = 0.8f), Color.Transparent ) ) ) ) } ```
## Dialogs If both the following conditions are true, then the Dialog is full screen and must be made edge-to-edge: 1. The `DialogProperties` contains `usePlatformDefaultWidth = false`. 2. The Dialog calls `Modifier.fillMaxSize()`. To make a full screen Dialog edge-to-edge, set `decorFitsSystemWindows = false` in the `DialogProperties`. ```kotlin Dialog( onDismissRequest = { /* Handle dismiss */ }, properties = DialogProperties( // 1. Allows the dialog to span the full width of the screen usePlatformDefaultWidth = false, // 2. Allows the dialog to draw behind status and navigation bars decorFitsSystemWindows = false ) ) { /* Content */ } ```
## Checklist - \[ \] Does every `Activity` call `enableEdgeToEdge()`? - \[ \] Is `adjustResize` set in the `AndroidManifest.xml`? - \[ \] Does every `TextField`, `OutlinedTextField`, or `BasicTextField` have a parent with `imePadding()`, `fitInside`, `Modifier.safeDrawingPadding()`, `Modifier.safeContentPadding()`, `Modifier.safeGesturesPadding()`, or `contentWindowInsets` set to `WindowInsets.safeDrawing` or `WindowInsets.ime`? - \[\] Does the first and last list item draw away from the system bars by passing insets to `contentPadding`? - \[\] Do FABs draw above the navigation bars by either being inside a Scaffold or by applying `Modifier.safeDrawingPadding()`? - \[\] Does the project build? Run `./gradlew build` to be sure.

skills.name: glance-appwidget-updates-and-memory
skills.desc: Manages Android AppWidget state updates, background syncs, and RemoteViews
skills.body:
--- name: glance-appwidget-updates-and-memory description: Manages Android AppWidget state updates, background syncs, and RemoteViews bitmap memory limits with Jetpack Glance (androidx.glance:glance-appwidget) and AppWidgetProvider receivers on Android 17 (API 37). Use this skill when configuring Android 17 (API level 37) compileSdk/targetSdk and AndroidManifest.xml widget receivers, refreshing frozen or stale Glance widget UI after CoroutineWorker DataStore preference updates (updateAppWidgetState), downsampling images within the WindowMetrics memory limit for SizeMode.Responsive, SizeMode.Exact, or LazyColumn, sharing content:// URIs with FileProvider, or fixing ActionCallback NoSuchMethodException and AppWidgetProvider ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException crashes with WorkManager. Don't use for Glance layout templates (suggest the glance-canonical-layouts skill) or in-app Compose screens. license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt metadata: author: Google LLC last-updated: '2026-11-12' keywords: - Android - AppWidget - Glance - GlanceAppWidget - GlanceAppWidgetReceiver - AppWidgetProvider - RemoteViews - widget memory limit - WindowMetrics - bitmap memory - SizeMode.Responsive - LazyColumn - ImageProvider - updateAppWidgetState - ActionCallback - NoSuchMethodException - R8 - ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException - WorkManager - CoroutineWorker - FileProvider - Android 17 - API 37 --- This skill provides guidance for managing state updates and keeping Android AppWidgets that use Jetpack Glance (`androidx.glance:glance-appwidget`) or `RemoteViews` within the Android 17 widget bitmap memory limits. For widget UI layout templates, suggest the `glance-canonical-layouts` skill. - When configuring a Glance widget, see [Create an app widget with Glance](references/android/develop/ui/compose/glance/create-app-widget.md). - When targeting Android 17 (`targetSdk = 37`), see [Android 17 widget memory limits](references/android/about/versions/17/behavior-changes-17.md). - When maintaining a classic `AppWidgetProvider`, see [Create an app widget](references/android/develop/ui/views/appwidgets/index.md). ## Prerequisites - Kotlin Android project (`minSdk >= 26`) with `compileSdk = 37` (`targetSdk = 37` when targeting Android 17) in `build.gradle.kts`. - Jetpack Glance (`1.2.0`, minimum `1.1.1+`) and the Compose compiler Gradle plugin enabled on the module. ## Critical mandates - **Preserve existing package name and toolchain versions** : Inspect `build.gradle.kts`, `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, and Kotlin files first. Keep existing `namespace`, `applicationId`, `package`, `targetSdk` (unless migrating to Android 17), Android Gradle Plugin (AGP), and Kotlin versions. - **Downsample images to widget dimensions and estimate the memory cap** : Android `system_server` computes the `RemoteViews` bitmap memory cap (`6 * width * height` bytes, or `1.5 * 4 * width * height`) once at boot from the real size of the default display and does not expose this cap in a public API. Because unfolding a foldable or switching display resolution to `QHD+` after boot can make active window metrics report a larger value than the boot-time cap, always downsample each image first to the widget's target dimensions (`maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` in `RGB_565` or `ALPHA_8`), and enforce the per-image byte ceiling (`calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes(context) / distinctImageCount`) estimated as `6 * width * height` from `WindowManager.currentWindowMetrics.bounds` on API 30+ (falling back to `resources.displayMetrics` on API 26-29 or if `WindowManager` is unavailable). - **Decode shared bitmaps once outside provideContent** : Both `SizeMode.Exact` (used by `glance-canonical-layouts` to compose the current span's portrait and landscape orientations) and `SizeMode.Responsive` (used to pre-bundle a set of `DpSize` breakpoints) invoke `provideContent` multiple times per update. Decode shared bitmaps once in `provideGlance` before `provideContent` and pass them to `ImageProvider(bitmap)` so `RemoteViews` deduplicates the shared `Bitmap` across all sizes in either mode. If a widget scales distinct bitmaps per `LocalSize.current`, divide `calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes(context)` by the number of distinct bitmaps. - **Prefer in-memory `Bitmap`s over `FileProvider` `content://` URIs** : On Android 17 (`targetSdk >= 37`), bitmap-backed `Icon`s count toward the cap alongside `Bitmap`s. Pass downsampled bitmaps directly in memory with `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(bitmap)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewBitmap` by default (`FileProvider` URI permission grants fail when a work-profile widget is placed on a personal home screen). Although `content://` URIs passed to `ImageProvider(uri)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewUri` don't count toward the inter-process communication (IPC) cap, the launcher decodes them at full resolution; if a widget must pass a `content://` URI, downsample the file into `context.cacheDir`, expose it with `FileProvider.getUriForFile`, and grant `Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION` to `Intent.CATEGORY_HOME` packages. - **Trigger explicit widget updates after state mutations** : `updateAppWidgetState` writes preferences to DataStore without updating the widget UI. After you mutate state, call `GlanceAppWidget.update(context, glanceId)` or `GlanceAppWidget.updateAll(context)`. - **Use full updateAppWidget calls when you replace images** : In `AppWidgetProvider` classes, when you replace bitmaps or `Icon`s, call `AppWidgetManager.updateAppWidget` instead of `partiallyUpdateAppWidget`. ## Reference implementation files Read the companion reference files in `references/` when implementing each step, and update the sample `package` declaration and class names to match your app: - **Bitmap Cap \& FileProvider Helper** : [WidgetBitmapUtils.kt](references/WidgetBitmapUtils.kt) - **Responsive Widget, Receiver \& Error Fallback** : [SampleGlanceWidget.kt](references/SampleGlanceWidget.kt) - **LazyColumn Collection Widget \& Revision Cache** : [FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt](references/FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt) - **DataStore State Push, CoroutineWorker \& ActionCallback** : [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt) - **Classic AppWidgetProvider WorkManager \& Full Update** : [ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt](references/ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt) - **Manifest, Widget Info, FileProvider Paths \& R8 Rules** : [AndroidManifest.xml](references/AndroidManifest.xml), [sample_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_widget_info.xml), [file_paths.xml](references/res/xml/file_paths.xml), [proguard-rules.pro](references/proguard-rules.pro) ## Detailed steps ### Step 1: Configure SDK levels, dependencies, and manifest declarations 1. Read `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `app/build.gradle.kts`, and `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` first. If AGP, Kotlin, or library versions are already present, keep them; otherwise, add `glance = "1.2.0"` along with `androidx.glance:glance-appwidget` and `androidx.glance:glance-material3` to `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. 2. In `app/build.gradle.kts`, keep `namespace`, `applicationId`, and any existing `minSdk >= 26`, `targetSdk`, or library versions. Set `compileSdk = 37` (and `targetSdk = 37` only when explicitly migrating the app to target Android 17), enable `buildFeatures { compose = true }`, and add `implementation(libs.androidx.glance.appwidget)` and `implementation(libs.androidx.glance.material3)`. 3. In `AndroidManifest.xml` (see [AndroidManifest.xml](references/AndroidManifest.xml)), register your `GlanceAppWidgetReceiver` (pointing `android.appwidget.provider` to `@xml/sample_widget_info`, see [sample_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_widget_info.xml)). If the widget must pass `content://` URIs with `cacheWidgetImageUri`, also declare `` with `` and `` (so `queryIntentActivities` discovers launcher packages on API 30+) and register `androidx.core.content.FileProvider` with `android:authorities="${applicationId}.fileprovider"`, `android:exported="false"`, `android:grantUriPermissions="true"`, and `android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS` pointing to `@xml/file_paths` (which declares ``, see [file_paths.xml](references/res/xml/file_paths.xml)):
```xml ```
### Step 2: Estimate the widget memory cap and downsample images Read [WidgetBitmapUtils.kt](references/WidgetBitmapUtils.kt) and implement the memory cap and downsampling helpers: 1. **Estimate the cap (`calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes`)** : On API 30+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R`), read `val bounds = context.getSystemService(WindowManager::class.java)?.currentWindowMetrics?.bounds` and, when `bounds != null && bounds.width() > 0 && bounds.height() > 0`, return `6L * bounds.width().toLong() * bounds.height().toLong()` (calling `WindowManager` from a non-UI widget or worker `Context` logs a nonfatal `StrictMode` violation on API 30+, which is expected for this estimate). On API 26-29 (or if `WindowManager` is unavailable), fall back to `context.resources.displayMetrics` (`6L * dm.widthPixels.toLong() * dm.heightPixels.toLong()`). Because `system_server` caches `6 * width * height` once at boot, always size images to the widget's `maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` first (Stage 1) rather than filling the full screen budget. 2. **Downsample in two stages (`decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap`)** : - First, probe dimensions with `BitmapFactory.Options().apply { inJustDecodeBounds = true; inPreferredConfig = config }` and double `sampleSize *= 2` while `(bounds.outWidth / (sampleSize * 2) >= targetWidthPx && bounds.outHeight / (sampleSize * 2) >= targetHeightPx) || (bounds.outWidth / sampleSize > targetWidthPx * 2) || (bounds.outHeight / sampleSize > targetHeightPx * 2)` (where `targetWidthPx = max(1, (maxWidthDp * density).toInt())`), so wide banners or tall screenshots do not bypass downsampling when one axis already fits. - Second, enforce the per-image byte ceiling (`perImageCapBytes = calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes(context) / max(1, distinctImageCount)`) by doubling `sampleSize *= 2` while `(max(1, bounds.outWidth / sampleSize).toLong() * max(1, bounds.outHeight / sampleSize).toLong() * bytesPerPixel) > perImageCapBytes`. Use `2L` bytes per pixel for `Bitmap.Config.RGB_565` (opaque photos), `1L` for `Bitmap.Config.ALPHA_8` masks, and `4L` when `bounds.outConfig != null && bounds.outConfig != config` (because `BitmapFactory` upgrades translucent PNG or WebP files from `RGB_565` to 4-byte `ARGB_8888`). Decode with `inSampleSize = sampleSize` and `inPreferredConfig = config`. 3. **Prefer in-memory `Bitmap` over `FileProvider` `Uri` (`cacheWidgetImageUri`)** : Prefer `decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap` with `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(bitmap)` (or `RemoteViews.setImageViewBitmap`) to pass downsampled bitmaps directly in memory (`FileProvider` URI permission grants fail when a work-profile widget is placed on a personal home screen). Only use `cacheWidgetImageUri` when an existing widget must pass a `content://` `Uri` to `ImageProvider(uri)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewUri`: it writes the downsampled bitmap into `File(context.cacheDir, "widget_images")`, obtains a `content://` URI with `FileProvider.getUriForFile(context, "${context.packageName}.fileprovider", outFile)`, queries `Intent(Intent.ACTION_MAIN).addCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_HOME)`, and calls `context.grantUriPermission(pkg, uri, Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION)`. ### Step 3: Deduplicate multi-size bitmaps and handle composition errors Read [SampleGlanceWidget.kt](references/SampleGlanceWidget.kt) to configure multi-size bitmap deduplication and composition error recovery: 1. **Choose `SizeMode` for your layout** : Use `SizeMode.Exact` (recommended when using `glance-canonical-layouts` to render exact `LocalSize.current` dimensions for the current grid span's portrait and landscape orientations), `SizeMode.Responsive(RESPONSIVE_BUCKETS)` (using `import androidx.compose.ui.unit.DpSize` and `import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp` to pre-bundle fixed `DpSize` breakpoints such as `setOf(DpSize(120.dp, 120.dp), DpSize(240.dp, 120.dp), DpSize(240.dp, 240.dp))` so resize transitions don't wake the app process), or `SizeMode.Single` (for a single layout). 2. **Hoist shared bitmap decodes before `provideContent`** : Because both `SizeMode.Exact` (`2-4` orientation sizes) and `SizeMode.Responsive` (`N` buckets) run `provideContent` multiple times per update, decode shared bitmaps once in `provideGlance` **before** `provideContent` with `decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap` and `Bitmap.Config.RGB_565` for opaque images (`distinctImageCount = 1`). Pass the resulting `Bitmap` to `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(sharedBitmap)` so `RemoteViews` deduplicates the shared `Bitmap` across all sizes. 3. **Provide a zero-bitmap error fallback** : Override `onCompositionError(context, glanceId, appWidgetId, throwable)` and call `AppWidgetManager.getInstance(context).updateAppWidget(appWidgetId, fallback)` with a text-only `RemoteViews` layout (`0` bitmaps). ### Step 4: Pre-decode LazyColumn collection images and assign stable itemIds Read [FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt](references/FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt) when rendering collection widgets with `LazyColumn`: 1. Replace `import androidx.glance.appwidget.ImageProvider` (which accepts `Uri`) with `import androidx.glance.ImageProvider` (which accepts `Bitmap`). Remove `Uri.fromFile` and `Icon.createWithContentUri` calls. 2. While a Glance session is active (\~45 seconds after an update), `.update()` and `.updateAll()` do not restart `provideGlance`. Declare `var cachedRevision = -1` and `var cachedThumbnails = emptyMap()` in `provideGlance` before `provideContent`. Inside `provideContent`, read `val revision = currentState()[KEY_REVISION] ?: 0`, and only when `revision != cachedRevision`, update `cachedRevision = revision` and decode the `feedItems` thumbnails with `cachedThumbnails = feedItems.mapNotNull { item -> decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap(..., distinctImageCount = max(1, feedItems.size), config = Bitmap.Config.RGB_565)?.let { item.id to it } }.toMap()` (use `mapNotNull` rather than `associate` so the map stays `Map` instead of `Map`). This re-decodes when DataStore state updates during an active session while sharing one decoded `Map` across all `SizeMode.Responsive` buckets. 3. In `LazyColumn`, pass a stable `Long` `itemId` to `items(items = feedItems, itemId = { item -> item.id.hashCode().toLong() })` (preferring a persistent numeric ID when available) and render `Image(provider = ImageProvider(bitmap), contentDescription = item.title)` only when `bitmap != null` (never fall back to `Uri.fromFile` in an `else` branch). ### Step 5: Push state updates, configure ActionCallbacks, and use WorkManager Read [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt), [proguard-rules.pro](references/proguard-rules.pro), and [ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt](references/ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt) to implement these patterns: 1. **Push DataStore updates** (requires `androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences-core:1.2.1` and `import androidx.glance.appwidget.GlanceAppWidgetManager`, `import androidx.glance.appwidget.state.updateAppWidgetState`, and `import androidx.glance.appwidget.updateAll`): In `pushWidgetRevisionUpdate(context)` (see [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt)), iterate over `for (glanceId in GlanceAppWidgetManager(context).getGlanceIds(Widget::class.java))`, mutate state inside `updateAppWidgetState(context, glanceId) { prefs -> ... }` (passing both `context` and `glanceId`), and immediately call `widget.update(context, glanceId)` (or `widget.updateAll(context)`). 2. **Use zero-argument `ActionCallback` classes with `ActionParameters.Key` and keep `()` under R8** (requires `androidx.work:work-runtime-ktx:2.12.0` when scheduling background work): `RunCallbackAction` instantiates `ActionCallback` classes with `Class.getDeclaredConstructor().newInstance()`, so a constructor parameter fails in every build. Remove constructor parameters from `ActionCallback` implementations, pass values with `ActionParameters.Key` and `actionParametersOf` (see `RefreshWidgetAction` in [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt)), and add `-keep class * implements androidx.glance.appwidget.action.ActionCallback { public (); }` to `proguard-rules.pro` (see [proguard-rules.pro](references/proguard-rules.pro)). Inside `SyncWidgetWorker.doWork()`, call `pushWidgetRevisionUpdate(applicationContext)` so background work updates DataStore and refreshes the widget. 3. **Avoid unconditional one-time `WorkManager` enqueues in `AppWidgetProvider.onUpdate` and use full `updateAppWidget` for images** (see [ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt](references/ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt)): Never call `context.startForegroundService` from `AppWidgetProvider.onReceive` or `onUpdate` (which throws `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`). `GlanceAppWidgetReceiver` already keeps a 10-year delayed session worker queued internally so WorkManager's `RescheduleReceiver` never toggles. In a classic `AppWidgetProvider`, avoid enqueuing a `OneTimeWorkRequest` directly inside `onUpdate`: even with `ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP`, once the one-time worker finishes (`SUCCEEDED`), `UnfinishedWorkListener` disables `RescheduleReceiver`, which broadcasts `ACTION_PACKAGE_CHANGED` and re-triggers `onUpdate` in a loop. Instead, schedule repeating syncs in `onUpdate` with `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(..., ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP, ...)` (which stays `ENQUEUED` across runs), use `goAsync()` for short `< 10s` updates, or enqueue one-time work (`enqueueUniqueWork(..., ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP, ...)`) only from specific action broadcasts in `onReceive`. When you update a `Bitmap` or `Icon` on a classic `RemoteViews` widget, call `appWidgetManager.updateAppWidget` rather than `partiallyUpdateAppWidget`. ## Common errors and fixes | Symptom or exception | Root cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | `IllegalArgumentException: RemoteViews for widget update exceeds maximum bitmap memory usage` | `RemoteViews` bitmap or icon memory exceeded `6 * W * H` bytes. | Downsample to the widget's `maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` with `inSampleSize` and `RGB_565` (or `ALPHA_8` for masks), enforce `calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes(context) / distinctImageCount`, and decode shared bitmaps once before `provideContent`. | | `SecurityException: Permission Denial: opening provider` or blank `content://` widget image | Home launcher lacks read permission for the `FileProvider` `content://` URI (including when a work-profile widget is placed on a personal home screen) or app passed `file://` with `Uri.fromFile`. | Prefer passing a downsampled `Bitmap` in memory with `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(bitmap)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewBitmap` (which also works across work profiles). If the widget must use a `content://` URI, expose the file with `FileProvider`, add `` for `CATEGORY_HOME`, and call `context.grantUriPermission` with `Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION`. | | Widget UI stays frozen after `updateAppWidgetState` | `updateAppWidgetState` writes to DataStore without recomposing, or `provideGlance` was not re-triggered during an active session. | Call `.update(context, glanceId)` or `.updateAll(context)` after `updateAppWidgetState`, and observe revision state inside `provideContent`. | | `NoSuchMethodException: . []` on action tap | `ActionCallback` declared constructor parameters or R8 stripped `()`. | Use a public zero-argument constructor, pass values with `ActionParameters.Key`, and keep `()` in ProGuard. | | `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` in receiver | `AppWidgetProvider` called `startForegroundService` in the background. | Schedule periodic syncs in `onUpdate` with `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork` (`ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP`) or enqueue one-time work (`enqueueUniqueWork`) from custom action broadcasts in `onReceive`. | | `Unresolved reference: ImageProvider`, `DpSize`, `updateAppWidgetState`, or `updateAll` | Missing or mismatched Glance and Compose package imports, or calling `updateAppWidgetState(context)` without `glanceId`. | Import `androidx.glance.ImageProvider` (for `Bitmap`), `androidx.compose.ui.unit.DpSize` and `androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp` (for `SizeMode.Responsive`), `androidx.glance.appwidget.state.updateAppWidgetState` (passing both `context` and `glanceId`), and `androidx.glance.appwidget.updateAll`. | ## Antipatterns - **NEVER** decode or scale a `Bitmap` inside `provideContent` per size bucket with `SizeMode.Responsive` or `SizeMode.Exact`. - **NEVER** size widget bitmaps to fill the full screen memory cap (`6 * width * height`); always downsample to the widget's target `maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` first so unfolding a foldable or switching display resolution after boot does not exceed the boot-time cap. - **NEVER** pass an unscaled `content://` `Uri` or `Uri.fromFile` to `ImageProvider(uri)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewUri`, or omit `context.grantUriPermission` for `Intent.CATEGORY_HOME`. - **NEVER** call `updateAppWidgetState` without calling `GlanceAppWidget.update(context, glanceId)` or `GlanceAppWidget.updateAll(context)`. - **NEVER** call `partiallyUpdateAppWidget` when you replace widget images.

After you mutate state, call `GlanceAppWidget.update(context, glanceId)` or `GlanceAppWidget.updateAll(context)`. - **Use full updateAppWidget calls when you replace images** : In `AppWidgetProvider` classes, when you replace bitmaps or `Icon`s, call `AppWidgetManager.updateAppWidget` instead of `partiallyUpdateAppWidget`. ## Reference implementation files Read the companion reference files in `references/` when implementing each step, and update the sample `package` declaration and class names to match your app: - **Bitmap Cap \& FileProvider Helper** : [WidgetBitmapUtils.kt](references/WidgetBitmapUtils.kt) - **Responsive Widget, Receiver \& Error Fallback** : [SampleGlanceWidget.kt](references/SampleGlanceWidget.kt) - **LazyColumn Collection Widget \& Revision Cache** : [FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt](references/FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt) - **DataStore State Push, CoroutineWorker \& ActionCallback** : [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt) - **Classic AppWidgetProvider WorkManager \& Full Update** : [ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt](references/ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt) - **Manifest, Widget Info, FileProvider Paths \& R8 Rules** : [AndroidManifest.xml](references/AndroidManifest.xml), [sample_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_widget_info.xml), [file_paths.xml](references/res/xml/file_paths.xml), [proguard-rules.pro](references/proguard-rules.pro) ## Detailed steps ### Step 1: Configure SDK levels, dependencies, and manifest declarations 1. Read `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, `app/build.gradle.kts`, and `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` first. If AGP, Kotlin, or library versions are already present, keep them; otherwise, add `glance = "1.2.0"` along with `androidx.glance:glance-appwidget` and `androidx.glance:glance-material3` to `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. 2. In `app/build.gradle.kts`, keep `namespace`, `applicationId`, and any existing `minSdk >= 26`, `targetSdk`, or library versions. Set `compileSdk = 37` (and `targetSdk = 37` only when explicitly migrating the app to target Android 17), enable `buildFeatures { compose = true }`, and add `implementation(libs.androidx.glance.appwidget)` and `implementation(libs.androidx.glance.material3)`. 3. In `AndroidManifest.xml` (see [AndroidManifest.xml](references/AndroidManifest.xml)), register your `GlanceAppWidgetReceiver` (pointing `android.appwidget.provider` to `@xml/sample_widget_info`, see [sample_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_widget_info.xml)). If the widget must pass `content://` URIs with `cacheWidgetImageUri`, also declare `` with `` and `` (so `queryIntentActivities` discovers launcher packages on API 30+) and register `androidx.core.content.FileProvider` with `android:authorities="${applicationId}.fileprovider"`, `android:exported="false"`, `android:grantUriPermissions="true"`, and `android.support.FILE_PROVIDER_PATHS` pointing to `@xml/file_paths` (which declares ``, see [file_paths.xml](references/res/xml/file_paths.xml)):
```xml ```
### Step 2: Estimate the widget memory cap and downsample images Read [WidgetBitmapUtils.kt](references/WidgetBitmapUtils.kt) and implement the memory cap and downsampling helpers: 1. **Estimate the cap (`calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes`)** : On API 30+ (`Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R`), read `val bounds = context.getSystemService(WindowManager::class.java)?.currentWindowMetrics?.bounds` and, when `bounds != null && bounds.width() > 0 && bounds.height() > 0`, return `6L * bounds.width().toLong() * bounds.height().toLong()` (calling `WindowManager` from a non-UI widget or worker `Context` logs a nonfatal `StrictMode` violation on API 30+, which is expected for this estimate). On API 26-29 (or if `WindowManager` is unavailable), fall back to `context.resources.displayMetrics` (`6L * dm.widthPixels.toLong() * dm.heightPixels.toLong()`). Because `system_server` caches `6 * width * height` once at boot, always size images to the widget's `maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` first (Stage 1) rather than filling the full screen budget. 2. **Downsample in two stages (`decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap`)** : - First, probe dimensions with `BitmapFactory.Options().apply { inJustDecodeBounds = true; inPreferredConfig = config }` and double `sampleSize *= 2` while `(bounds.outWidth / (sampleSize * 2) >= targetWidthPx && bounds.outHeight / (sampleSize * 2) >= targetHeightPx) || (bounds.outWidth / sampleSize > targetWidthPx * 2) || (bounds.outHeight / sampleSize > targetHeightPx * 2)` (where `targetWidthPx = max(1, (maxWidthDp * density).toInt())`), so wide banners or tall screenshots do not bypass downsampling when one axis already fits. - Second, enforce the per-image byte ceiling (`perImageCapBytes = calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes(context) / max(1, distinctImageCount)`) by doubling `sampleSize *= 2` while `(max(1, bounds.outWidth / sampleSize).toLong() * max(1, bounds.outHeight / sampleSize).toLong() * bytesPerPixel) > perImageCapBytes`. Use `2L` bytes per pixel for `Bitmap.Config.RGB_565` (opaque photos), `1L` for `Bitmap.Config.ALPHA_8` masks, and `4L` when `bounds.outConfig != null && bounds.outConfig != config` (because `BitmapFactory` upgrades translucent PNG or WebP files from `RGB_565` to 4-byte `ARGB_8888`). Decode with `inSampleSize = sampleSize` and `inPreferredConfig = config`. 3. **Prefer in-memory `Bitmap` over `FileProvider` `Uri` (`cacheWidgetImageUri`)** : Prefer `decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap` with `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(bitmap)` (or `RemoteViews.setImageViewBitmap`) to pass downsampled bitmaps directly in memory (`FileProvider` URI permission grants fail when a work-profile widget is placed on a personal home screen). Only use `cacheWidgetImageUri` when an existing widget must pass a `content://` `Uri` to `ImageProvider(uri)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewUri`: it writes the downsampled bitmap into `File(context.cacheDir, "widget_images")`, obtains a `content://` URI with `FileProvider.getUriForFile(context, "${context.packageName}.fileprovider", outFile)`, queries `Intent(Intent.ACTION_MAIN).addCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_HOME)`, and calls `context.grantUriPermission(pkg, uri, Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION)`. ### Step 3: Deduplicate multi-size bitmaps and handle composition errors Read [SampleGlanceWidget.kt](references/SampleGlanceWidget.kt) to configure multi-size bitmap deduplication and composition error recovery: 1. **Choose `SizeMode` for your layout** : Use `SizeMode.Exact` (recommended when using `glance-canonical-layouts` to render exact `LocalSize.current` dimensions for the current grid span's portrait and landscape orientations), `SizeMode.Responsive(RESPONSIVE_BUCKETS)` (using `import androidx.compose.ui.unit.DpSize` and `import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp` to pre-bundle fixed `DpSize` breakpoints such as `setOf(DpSize(120.dp, 120.dp), DpSize(240.dp, 120.dp), DpSize(240.dp, 240.dp))` so resize transitions don't wake the app process), or `SizeMode.Single` (for a single layout). 2. **Hoist shared bitmap decodes before `provideContent`** : Because both `SizeMode.Exact` (`2-4` orientation sizes) and `SizeMode.Responsive` (`N` buckets) run `provideContent` multiple times per update, decode shared bitmaps once in `provideGlance` **before** `provideContent` with `decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap` and `Bitmap.Config.RGB_565` for opaque images (`distinctImageCount = 1`). Pass the resulting `Bitmap` to `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(sharedBitmap)` so `RemoteViews` deduplicates the shared `Bitmap` across all sizes. 3. **Provide a zero-bitmap error fallback** : Override `onCompositionError(context, glanceId, appWidgetId, throwable)` and call `AppWidgetManager.getInstance(context).updateAppWidget(appWidgetId, fallback)` with a text-only `RemoteViews` layout (`0` bitmaps). ### Step 4: Pre-decode LazyColumn collection images and assign stable itemIds Read [FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt](references/FeedCollectionGlanceWidget.kt) when rendering collection widgets with `LazyColumn`: 1. Replace `import androidx.glance.appwidget.ImageProvider` (which accepts `Uri`) with `import androidx.glance.ImageProvider` (which accepts `Bitmap`). Remove `Uri.fromFile` and `Icon.createWithContentUri` calls. 2. While a Glance session is active (\~45 seconds after an update), `.update()` and `.updateAll()` do not restart `provideGlance`. Declare `var cachedRevision = -1` and `var cachedThumbnails = emptyMap()` in `provideGlance` before `provideContent`. Inside `provideContent`, read `val revision = currentState()[KEY_REVISION] ?: 0`, and only when `revision != cachedRevision`, update `cachedRevision = revision` and decode the `feedItems` thumbnails with `cachedThumbnails = feedItems.mapNotNull { item -> decodeDownsampledWidgetBitmap(..., distinctImageCount = max(1, feedItems.size), config = Bitmap.Config.RGB_565)?.let { item.id to it } }.toMap()` (use `mapNotNull` rather than `associate` so the map stays `Map` instead of `Map`). This re-decodes when DataStore state updates during an active session while sharing one decoded `Map` across all `SizeMode.Responsive` buckets. 3. In `LazyColumn`, pass a stable `Long` `itemId` to `items(items = feedItems, itemId = { item -> item.id.hashCode().toLong() })` (preferring a persistent numeric ID when available) and render `Image(provider = ImageProvider(bitmap), contentDescription = item.title)` only when `bitmap != null` (never fall back to `Uri.fromFile` in an `else` branch). ### Step 5: Push state updates, configure ActionCallbacks, and use WorkManager Read [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt), [proguard-rules.pro](references/proguard-rules.pro), and [ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt](references/ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt) to implement these patterns: 1. **Push DataStore updates** (requires `androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences-core:1.2.1` and `import androidx.glance.appwidget.GlanceAppWidgetManager`, `import androidx.glance.appwidget.state.updateAppWidgetState`, and `import androidx.glance.appwidget.updateAll`): In `pushWidgetRevisionUpdate(context)` (see [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt)), iterate over `for (glanceId in GlanceAppWidgetManager(context).getGlanceIds(Widget::class.java))`, mutate state inside `updateAppWidgetState(context, glanceId) { prefs -> ... }` (passing both `context` and `glanceId`), and immediately call `widget.update(context, glanceId)` (or `widget.updateAll(context)`). 2. **Use zero-argument `ActionCallback` classes with `ActionParameters.Key` and keep `()` under R8** (requires `androidx.work:work-runtime-ktx:2.12.0` when scheduling background work): `RunCallbackAction` instantiates `ActionCallback` classes with `Class.getDeclaredConstructor().newInstance()`, so a constructor parameter fails in every build. Remove constructor parameters from `ActionCallback` implementations, pass values with `ActionParameters.Key` and `actionParametersOf` (see `RefreshWidgetAction` in [WidgetStateAndActions.kt](references/WidgetStateAndActions.kt)), and add `-keep class * implements androidx.glance.appwidget.action.ActionCallback { public (); }` to `proguard-rules.pro` (see [proguard-rules.pro](references/proguard-rules.pro)). Inside `SyncWidgetWorker.doWork()`, call `pushWidgetRevisionUpdate(applicationContext)` so background work updates DataStore and refreshes the widget. 3. **Avoid unconditional one-time `WorkManager` enqueues in `AppWidgetProvider.onUpdate` and use full `updateAppWidget` for images** (see [ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt](references/ClassicWidgetImageUpdater.kt)): Never call `context.startForegroundService` from `AppWidgetProvider.onReceive` or `onUpdate` (which throws `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException`). `GlanceAppWidgetReceiver` already keeps a 10-year delayed session worker queued internally so WorkManager's `RescheduleReceiver` never toggles. In a classic `AppWidgetProvider`, avoid enqueuing a `OneTimeWorkRequest` directly inside `onUpdate`: even with `ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP`, once the one-time worker finishes (`SUCCEEDED`), `UnfinishedWorkListener` disables `RescheduleReceiver`, which broadcasts `ACTION_PACKAGE_CHANGED` and re-triggers `onUpdate` in a loop. Instead, schedule repeating syncs in `onUpdate` with `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(..., ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP, ...)` (which stays `ENQUEUED` across runs), use `goAsync()` for short `< 10s` updates, or enqueue one-time work (`enqueueUniqueWork(..., ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP, ...)`) only from specific action broadcasts in `onReceive`. When you update a `Bitmap` or `Icon` on a classic `RemoteViews` widget, call `appWidgetManager.updateAppWidget` rather than `partiallyUpdateAppWidget`. ## Common errors and fixes | Symptom or exception | Root cause | Fix | |---|---|---| | `IllegalArgumentException: RemoteViews for widget update exceeds maximum bitmap memory usage` | `RemoteViews` bitmap or icon memory exceeded `6 * W * H` bytes. | Downsample to the widget's `maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` with `inSampleSize` and `RGB_565` (or `ALPHA_8` for masks), enforce `calculateWidgetMemoryCapBytes(context) / distinctImageCount`, and decode shared bitmaps once before `provideContent`. | | `SecurityException: Permission Denial: opening provider` or blank `content://` widget image | Home launcher lacks read permission for the `FileProvider` `content://` URI (including when a work-profile widget is placed on a personal home screen) or app passed `file://` with `Uri.fromFile`. | Prefer passing a downsampled `Bitmap` in memory with `androidx.glance.ImageProvider(bitmap)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewBitmap` (which also works across work profiles). If the widget must use a `content://` URI, expose the file with `FileProvider`, add `` for `CATEGORY_HOME`, and call `context.grantUriPermission` with `Intent.FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION`. | | Widget UI stays frozen after `updateAppWidgetState` | `updateAppWidgetState` writes to DataStore without recomposing, or `provideGlance` was not re-triggered during an active session. | Call `.update(context, glanceId)` or `.updateAll(context)` after `updateAppWidgetState`, and observe revision state inside `provideContent`. | | `NoSuchMethodException: . []` on action tap | `ActionCallback` declared constructor parameters or R8 stripped `()`. | Use a public zero-argument constructor, pass values with `ActionParameters.Key`, and keep `()` in ProGuard. | | `ForegroundServiceStartNotAllowedException` in receiver | `AppWidgetProvider` called `startForegroundService` in the background. | Schedule periodic syncs in `onUpdate` with `enqueueUniquePeriodicWork` (`ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP`) or enqueue one-time work (`enqueueUniqueWork`) from custom action broadcasts in `onReceive`. | | `Unresolved reference: ImageProvider`, `DpSize`, `updateAppWidgetState`, or `updateAll` | Missing or mismatched Glance and Compose package imports, or calling `updateAppWidgetState(context)` without `glanceId`. | Import `androidx.glance.ImageProvider` (for `Bitmap`), `androidx.compose.ui.unit.DpSize` and `androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp` (for `SizeMode.Responsive`), `androidx.glance.appwidget.state.updateAppWidgetState` (passing both `context` and `glanceId`), and `androidx.glance.appwidget.updateAll`. | ## Antipatterns - **NEVER** decode or scale a `Bitmap` inside `provideContent` per size bucket with `SizeMode.Responsive` or `SizeMode.Exact`. - **NEVER** size widget bitmaps to fill the full screen memory cap (`6 * width * height`); always downsample to the widget's target `maxWidthDp x maxHeightDp` first so unfolding a foldable or switching display resolution after boot does not exceed the boot-time cap. - **NEVER** pass an unscaled `content://` `Uri` or `Uri.fromFile` to `ImageProvider(uri)` or `RemoteViews.setImageViewUri`, or omit `context.grantUriPermission` for `Intent.CATEGORY_HOME`. - **NEVER** call `updateAppWidgetState` without calling `GlanceAppWidget.update(context, glanceId)` or `GlanceAppWidget.updateAll(context)`. - **NEVER** call `partiallyUpdateAppWidget` when you replace widget images.

--- name: glance-canonical-layouts description: Use this skill to create home screen widgets using Jetpack Glance Canonical Layouts from the Android Platform Samples project, or when asked to implement standard widget layout patterns (including Check List, Image Grid, Snap Scrolling, and Standard Toolbar). license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt metadata: author: Google LLC last-updated: '2026-11-18' keywords: - android - glance - widgets - appwidget - canonical-layouts - platform-samples - action-list - check-list - image-grid - image-text-list - snap-scrolling - full-bleed - expressive-toolbar - search-toolbar - standard-toolbar --- To implement a widget Canonical Layout that follows the recommended design patterns: 1. The project **MUST** use Jetpack Glance. 2. You **MUST** locate the requested layout from the list under **Canonical Layout Reference Files**. 3. Copy the layout reference files into your project's target app module (e.g., `src/main/java/` and `src/main/res/`) in one step to implement the exact design and reduce the number of tool calls. 4. You **MUST** set override val `sizeMode: SizeMode = SizeMode.Exact` in the widget provider class. 5. Validate that your project compiles, updating sample package declarations, import paths, and class names to match the target app's package name. 6. Clean your project's widget code, removing unused classes (for example, unused buttons). 7. You **MUST** register the widget receiver in `AndroidManifest.xml` inside `` after ``, ensuring `android:resource="@xml/..."` matches the filename of the copied Widget Info XML. Otherwise, the widget won't appear in the widget picker:
```xml ```
## Dependencies Add Jetpack Glance dependencies to the app module's `build.gradle.kts` (`dependencies` block): - `androidx.glance:glance-appwidget:1.2.0` or higher - `androidx.glance:glance-material3:1.2.0` or higher - `androidx.glance:glance-appwidget-preview:1.2.0` or higher - `androidx.glance:glance-preview:1.2.0` or higher Use version `1.3.0-alpha02` or higher with `compileSdk = 37` and Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 9.1.0 or higher (for example, `agp = "9.1.0"` in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`) when implementing Snap Scrolling. If copying sample data repositories that load bitmaps with Coil (such as `FakeImageGridDataRepository.kt`, `FakeImageTextListDataRepository.kt`, or `FakeTextWithImageRepository.kt`), also add an image loading library dependency such as `io.coil-kt:coil` (e.g., `implementation("io.coil-kt:coil:2.7.0")`) if one doesn't already exist. If copying `FontUtils.kt` (for long text, full-bleed image, or text with image layouts), also add `androidx.appcompat:appcompat`. For example, add `implementation("androidx.appcompat:appcompat:1.8.0")` if it doesn't already exist. `FontUtils.kt` uses `AppCompatTextView` so text auto-sizing also works below API level 27. ## Canonical layout reference files #### Action list layout (`action_list`) - **Widget Provider** : [ActionListAppWidget.kt](references/collections/ActionListAppWidget.kt) - **Layout Composable** : [ActionListLayout.kt](references/collections/layout/ActionListLayout.kt) - **Widget Info XML** : [sample_action_list_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_action_list_widget_info.xml) - **Data Repository** : [FakeActionListDataRepository.kt](references/collections/data/FakeActionListDataRepository.kt) - **Dimensions** : [dimens.xml](references/res/values/dimens.xml) - **Strings** : [strings.xml](references/res/values/strings.xml) - **Drawables** : [sample_action_list_preview.png](https://developer.android.com/static/agents/skills/system/glance-canonical-layouts/references/res/drawable-nodpi/sample_action_list_preview.png), [sample_home_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_home_icon.xml), [sample_power_settings_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_power_settings_icon.xml), [sample_bulb_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_bulb_icon.xml), [sample_thermostat_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_thermostat_icon.xml), [sample_ac_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_ac_icon.xml), [sample_door_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_door_icon.xml), [sample_arrow_right_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_arrow_right_icon.xml), [sample_no_data_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_no_data_icon.xml), [sample_add_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_add_icon.xml) - **Components** : [RoundedScrollingLazyVerticalGrid.kt](references/collections/layout/RoundedScrollingLazyVerticalGrid.kt), [ListItem.kt](references/collections/layout/ListItem.kt), [VerticalListItem.kt](references/collections/layout/VerticalListItem.kt), [RoundedScrollingLazyColumn.kt](references/collections/layout/RoundedScrollingLazyColumn.kt), [EmptyListContent.kt](references/collections/layout/EmptyListContent.kt), [NoDataContent.kt](references/collections/layout/NoDataContent.kt) - **Utilities** : [CollectionsKtx.kt](references/CollectionsKtx.kt), [ActionUtils.kt](references/utils/ActionUtils.kt), [PreviewAnnotations.kt](references/utils/PreviewAnnotations.kt) - **Theme** : [Color.kt](references/ui/theme/Color.kt), [Theme.kt](references/ui/theme/Theme.kt), [Type.kt](references/ui/theme/Type.kt) - **Additional References** : [CanonicalLayoutActivity.kt](references/CanonicalLayoutActivity.kt), [ActionDemonstrationActivity.kt](references/ActionDemonstrationActivity.kt) - **Guidance** : - Handle list item actions with Glance action callbacks and ensure proper state updates. #### Check list layout (`check_list`) - **Components** : [ListItem.kt](references/collections/layout/ListItem.kt), [VerticalListItem.kt](references/collections/layout/VerticalListItem.kt), [RoundedScrollingLazyColumn.kt](references/collections/layout/RoundedScrollingLazyColumn.kt), [EmptyListContent.kt](references/collections/layout/EmptyListContent.kt), [NoDataContent.kt](references/collections/layout/NoDataContent.kt) - **Guidance** : - Implement checkbox state toggling using action parameters or callbacks to update collection items. - Use Glance Action callbacks (for example, `actionRunCallback`, `ActionCallback(actionParametersOf(...)` or `actionStartActivity(...)`) for widget onClick parameters to handle click events like tapping a checkbox. #### Expressive toolbar layout (`expressive_toolbar`) - **Widget Provider** : [ExpressiveToolbarAppWidget.kt](references/toolbars/ExpressiveToolbarAppWidget.kt) - **Layout Composable** : [ExpressiveToolbarLayout.kt](references/toolbars/layout/ExpressiveToolbarLayout.kt) - **Widget Info XML** : [sample_expressive_toolbar_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_expressive_toolbar_widget_info.xml) - **Dimensions** : [dimens.xml](references/res/values/dimens.xml) - **Strings** : [strings.xml](references/res/values/strings.xml) - **Drawables** : [sample_expressive_toolbar_preview.png](https://developer.android.com/static/agents/skills/system/glance-canonical-layouts/references/res/drawable-nodpi/sample_expressive_toolbar_preview.png), [four_side_cookie_background.xml](references/res/drawable/four_side_cookie_background.xml), [sample_edit_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_edit_icon.xml), [sample_share_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_share_icon.xml), [sample_delete_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_delete_icon.xml), [sample_info_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_info_icon.xml), [sample_add_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_add_icon.xml), [sample_file_upload_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_file_upload_icon.xml), [sample_mic_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_mic_icon.xml), [sample_camera_icon.xml](references/res/drawable/sample_camera_icon.xml) - **Components** : [Buttons.kt](references/toolbars/layout/Buttons.kt), [LayoutComponents.kt](references/toolbars/layout/LayoutComponents.kt) - **Utilities** : [ActionUtils.kt](references/utils/ActionUtils.kt), [PreviewAnnotations.kt](references/utils/PreviewAnnotations.kt) - **Theme** : [Color.kt](references/ui/theme/Color.kt), [Theme.kt](references/ui/theme/Theme.kt), [Type.kt](references/ui/theme/Type.kt) - **Guidance** : - Avoid `ColorProvider` import errors: import `androidx.glance.unit.ColorProvider` and use `androidx.glance.color.ColorProvider(dayColor, nightColor)`. - Use `GlanceModifier.background(Color)` directly for solid background colors rather than `ColorProvider`. #### Image grid layout (`image_grid`) - **Widget Provider** : [ImageGridAppWidget.kt](references/collections/ImageGridAppWidget.kt) - **Layout Composable** : [ImageGridLayout.kt](references/collections/layout/ImageGridLayout.kt) - **Widget Info XML** : [sample_image_grid_widget_info.xml](references/res/xml/sample_image_grid_widget_info.xml) - To implement a widget Canonical Layout that follows the recommended design patterns: 1. The project **MUST** use Jetpack Glance. 2. You **MUST** locate the requested layout from the list under **Canonical Layout Reference Files**. 3. Copy the layout reference files into your project's target app module (e.g., `src/main/java/` and `src/main/res/`) in one step to implement the exact design and reduce the number of tool calls. 4. You **MUST** set override val `sizeMode: SizeMode = SizeMode.Exact` in the widget provider class. 5. Validate that your project compiles, updating sample package declarations, import paths, and class names to match the target app's package name. 6. Clean your project's widget code, removing unused classes (for example, unused buttons). 7. You **MUST** register the widget receiver in `AndroidManifest.xml` inside `` after ``, ensuring `android:resource="@xml/..."` matches the filename of the copied Widget Info XML. Otherwise, the widget won't appear in the widget picker:

## Dependencies Add Jetpack Glance dependencies to the app module's `build.gradle.kts` (`dependencies` block): - `androidx.glance:glance-appwidget:1.2.0` or higher - `androidx.glance:glance-material3:1.2.0` or higher - `androidx.glance:glance-appwidget-preview:1.2.0` or higher - `androidx.glance:glance-preview:1.2.0` or higher Use version `1.3.0-alpha02` or higher with `compileSdk = 37` and Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 9.1.0 or higher (for example, `agp = "9.1.0"` in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`) when implementing Snap Scrolling. If copying sample data repositories that load bitmaps with Coil (such as `FakeImageGridDataRepository.kt`, `FakeImageTextListDataRepository.kt`, or `FakeTextWithImageRepository.kt`), also add an image loading library dependency such as `io.coil-kt:coil` (e.g., `implementation("io.coil-kt:coil:2.7.0")`) if one doesn't already exist. If copying `FontUtils.kt` (for long text, full-bleed image, or text with image layouts), also add `androidx.appcompat:appcompat`. For example, add `implementation("androidx.appcompat:appcompat:1.8.0")` if it doesn't already exist. `FontUtils.kt` uses `AppCompatTextView` so text auto-sizing also works below API level 27. ## Canonical layout reference files #### Action list layout (`action_list`) - skills.name: testing-setup
skills.desc: Analyze and create a testing strategy for Android apps - install testing
skills.body:
---
name: testing-setup
description: Analyze and create a testing strategy for Android apps - install testing
  libraries, set up test infrastructure, create harnesses for unit tests, UI tests,
  screenshot tests, and end-to-end tests.
license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
metadata:
  author: Google LLC
  last-updated: '2026-11-20'
  keywords:
  - android
  - testing
  - ui tests
  - screenshot tests
  - coverage
---

## Step 1: Analyze the current testing setup

To understand the testing setup of an existing project, look for these
dependencies in the libs.versions.toml file, or build files:

1. Dependency Injection framework used. For example, Hilt, Koin, Anvil, or vanilla Dagger.
2. Unit (local) testing framework this project uses. For example, JUnit4 or JUnit5.
3. Mocking framework (if any) used for unit tests, and for instrumented and UI tests. For example, Mockito or Mockk.
4. Robolectric. Identify which of these three uses apply:
   1. Used in unit tests to have fakes for platform entities
   2. To run behavior UI tests without a device or emulator. For example, used to run Espresso or Compose tests.
   3. To do screenshot testing with Roborazzi
5. Is the app 100% Compose, Views or hybrid?
6. Behavior UI tests:
   1. Compose Tests (`androidx.compose.ui:ui-test-*`)
   2. Espresso Tests for Views. Check for wrappers such as Kaspresso. Dependencies: `androidx.test.espresso:espresso-core`, `androidx.test:runner`, `androidx.test:rules`.
7. Screenshot tests. Identify which of these types the project uses:
   1. Instrumented (device-based). For example, using Dropshots.
   2. Based on Robolectric, so they run locally. For example, using Roborazzi.
   3. Based on LayoutLib, so they run locally. For example, Paparazzi, or the Compose Preview Screenshot Testing tool.
8. End to end tests (also known as Release Candidate tests) always run on device and use high-level frameworks such as UIAutomator, Appium, or Robotium.
9. Generate a Markdown report with the analysis

## Step 2: Set up Dependency Injection frameworks for testing

If there is no Dependency Injection framework, install one: if it's a
multiplatform application, ask the user whether they want to install Koin, or
kotlin-inject. If it's not multiplatform, install Hilt.

Install the testing dependencies (for example `com.google.dagger:hilt-compiler`
that should be applied with a `kspAndroidTest` configuration).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Important:** Always consult the documentation of the applicable framework to learn about testing (for example: [Hilt testing guide](references/android/training/dependency-injection/hilt-testing.md), [Koin Instrumented tests](https://insert-koin.io/docs/reference/koin-android/instrumented-testing)).

For instrumented tests, create and configure (by adding
`testInstrumentationRunner` to the build gradle files) a new test runner and
apply the testing rules required by the framework (for example in Hilt, annotate
your test classes with `@HiltAndroidTest` and apply the `HiltAndroidRule`).
Other frameworks use other mechanisms, consult their documentation.

## Step 3: Install frameworks

Unless otherwise specified, respect the current stack of testing frameworks.

If there are no testing frameworks, and the user didn't specify any preference,
install the following:

- JUnit4 for local and instrumented tests
- JaCoCo for test coverage
- For UI tests: if the project has views, Espresso. If it's fully Compose, use the Compose Testing APIs.
- Robolectric to run UI Tests
- Compose Preview Screenshot Testing tool for screenshot tests. Check the
  project's AGP version first, then pick the matching setup and follow it
  strictly:

  - **AGP 9.5.0-alpha03 or higher (recommended):** configure an AGP test suite using `testOptions { screenshotTests.create(...) }`, as described in [Screenshot testing with test suites](references/android/studio/preview/compose-screenshot-testing-with-testsuites.md).
  - **Lower AGP versions:** use the [legacy standalone plugin setup](references/android/studio/preview/compose-screenshot-testing.md) with `com.android.compose.screenshot`, and tell the user it's deprecated. Don't upgrade AGP as part of setting up screenshot tests. Mention that test suites are available on 9.5.0-alpha03 or higher, and leave the upgrade as a separate decision.

  Don't combine both setups in the same module. If the project already uses
  the standalone plugin and its AGP version supports test suites, offer to
  migrate it using the tasks and paths mapping table in
  [Screenshot testing with test suites](references/android/studio/preview/compose-screenshot-testing-with-testsuites.md).
- Dropshots for device screenshot tests

- If a mocking framework is necessary, install Mockk (`io.mockk:mockk`). Do
  not install it unless it is clearly necessary.

If instrumented screenshot tests are requested, install Dropshots.

If end-to-end testing is requested, install UI Automator.

## Step 4: Refactor and create fakes for testing

### **Refactor for unit tests**

In the next sections you'll be asked to create tests. If you have dependencies
on Android framework classes, or entities that are not part of the codebase:

- First, use a fake. If it doesn't exist, create an interface for the class
  and a "Default" implementation with the existing code. Add the Fake version
  to the test sourceset (test or androidTest).

- If not possible to use a fake (example: no access to the class or
  interface), mock the dependencies.

### **Refactor for UI tests**

If you need to fake components to make testing easier and faster and more
reliable, replace slow and problematic dependencies with fakes. Use runtime
fakes using the Dependency Injection framework installed to:

- **Simulate** different scenarios with the user (wrong credentials or a password reset flow), with a server (no connection, server down, or bad JSON from the server) or with a platform component (insufficient permissions, no disk space, no front camera available)
- **Improve** speed and reliability (replacing a database with an in-memory database, replacing a repository with an in-memory fake to avoid hitting the network)

## Step 5: Unit testing

Create a task to add or review unit tests in every file that contains business
logic (ViewModels, Repositories, and database-related classes such as DAOs).
Don't create unit tests for Activities, Compose layouts, or dependency injection
configuration files.

## Step 6: UI testing

Espresso or Compose UI tests live in the `test` sourceset because they will be
run with Robolectric. If instrumented (emulator or device) tests are requested,
put them in the `androidTest` sourceset.

## Step 7: Test databases

If the database is using SQLite (through a library such as Room or SQLDelight),
create instrumented tests using an in-memory database to make sure that they
work with the SQLite engine on device.

## Step 8: Screenshot tests

Regardless of the framework used, screenshot tests focus on two types of tests:

- Screen-level screenshot tests, where each screen is tested in nine different sizes, combining compact, medium and expanded widths (400, 610, 900 dp) and heights (400, 500 and 1000 dp).
- Screen-level variations. Add a mobile (400x500) screenshot of:
  - All the alternative themes, if used.
  - Font scale set to 1.5.
- Component-level screenshot tests, where each component is tested in different themes and font scales.

Behavior isn't tested with screenshots, but do test different common scenarios
if their UIs change a lot depending on the state. For example, test loading
screens by injecting a loading state to the UI or simulating it with a fake.

## Step 9: UI Behavior tests

Test the UI logic using behavior tests, which ensures that the UIs react as
expected when different states are passed, and when user actions are performed.

### **Compose UI behavior tests**

- Use the ComposeTestRule with a `ComponentActivity` to access resources such as strings.
- Always match with semantic matchers first. If the matcher is too complicated to write (using more than three matchers to find a single element), use `testTag`.
- Always verify state restoration.

### **Views (XML) UI behavior tests**

Use Espresso to match views and interact with them.

## Step 10: Navigation tests

Create a test suite to verify navigation logic. Include:

- Back handling
- Deeplinks
- Special patterns like "exit through home" with multiple backstacks.

## Step 11: Simulate different window sizes and settings

For Compose layouts, use `DeviceConfigurationOverride` described in "[UI testing
common patterns](references/android/develop/ui/compose/testing/common-patterns.md)" to simulate different window sizes, font scales

## Step 12: End-to-end tests

Create a low number (about 5% of all tests) of end-to-end tests that cover big
user journeys. Use Compose Test APIs or Espresso for that. If you have to access
platform features such as notifications or system UI, use UI Automator.

If you need to take screenshots of the app running in a device, use
[Dropshots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dropbox/dropshots/refs/heads/main/README.md). You need a device for screenshot tests when verifying
interaction with the system UI (examples: edge-to-edge rendering, notifications,
picture-in-picture)

## Step 13: Instrumented Screenshot tests

Install the `com.dropbox.dropshots` plugin in the module and a `Dropshots()`
JUnit Rule. Create a new instrumented screenshot test for one of the app's
features.

## Step 14: Install JaCoCo

Install JaCoCo for local testing code coverage.

- Add the `jacoco` plugin to each module that contains tests.

## Final touches

- Ask whether to document the findings of the analysis and the changes applied
  to the testing strategy. If the user agrees:

  - If there is an AGENTS.md file present in the project, update it with any
    changes you've made to the testing strategy.

  - If there is no AGENTS.md file, create a new file (docs/testing.md) with
    a description of the testing strategy, including the commands needed to
    run every type of test and where the screenshot reference files live.
    Also create a new AGENTS.md file in the root and create a link to
    docs/testing.md.

Don't create unit tests for Activities, Compose layouts, or dependency injection
configuration files.

## Step 6: UI testing

Espresso or Compose UI tests live in the `test` sourceset because they will be
run with Robolectric. If instrumented (emulator or device) tests are requested,
put them in the `androidTest` sourceset.

## Step 7: Test databases

If the database is using SQLite (through a library such as Room or SQLDelight),
create instrumented tests using an in-memory database to make sure that they
work with the SQLite engine on device.

## Step 8: Screenshot tests

Regardless of the framework used, screenshot tests focus on two types of tests:

- Screen-level screenshot tests, where each screen is tested in nine different sizes, combining compact, medium and expanded widths (400, 610, 900 dp) and heights (400, 500 and 1000 dp).
- Screen-level variations. Add a mobile (400x500) screenshot of:
  - All the alternative themes, if used.
  - Font scale set to 1.5.
- Component-level screenshot tests, where each component is tested in different themes and font scales.

Behavior isn't tested with screenshots, but do test different common scenarios
if their UIs change a lot depending on the state. For example, test loading
screens by injecting a loading state to the UI or simulating it with a fake.

## Step 9: UI Behavior tests

Test the UI logic using behavior tests, which ensures that the UIs react as
expected when different states are passed, and when user actions are performed.

### **Compose UI behavior tests**

- Use the ComposeTestRule with a `ComponentActivity` to access resources such as strings.
- Always match with semantic matchers first. If the matcher is too complicated to write (using more than three matchers to find a single element), use `testTag`.
- Always verify state restoration.

### **Views (XML) UI behavior tests**

Use Espresso to match views and interact with them.

## Step 10: Navigation tests

Create a test suite to verify navigation logic. Include:

- Back handling
- Deeplinks
- Special patterns like "exit through home" with multiple backstacks.

## Step 11: Simulate different window sizes and settings

For Compose layouts, use `DeviceConfigurationOverride` described in "[UI testing
common patterns](references/android/develop/ui/compose/testing/common-patterns.md)" to simulate different window sizes, font scales

## Step 12: End-to-end tests

Create a low number (about 5% of all tests) of end-to-end tests that cover big
user journeys. Use Compose Test APIs or Espresso for that. If you have to access
platform features such as notifications or system UI, use UI Automator.

If you need to take screenshots of the app running in a device, use
[Dropshots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dropbox/dropshots/refs/heads/main/README.md). You need a device for screenshot tests when verifying
interaction with the system UI (examples: edge-to-edge rendering, notifications,
picture-in-picture)

## Step 13: Instrumented Screenshot tests

Install the `com.dropbox.dropshots` plugin in the module and a `Dropshots()`
JUnit Rule. Create a new instrumented screenshot test for one of the app's
features.

## Step 14: Install JaCoCo

Install JaCoCo for local testing code coverage.

- Add the `jacoco` plugin to each module that contains tests.

## Final touches

- Ask whether to document the findings of the analysis and the changes applied
  to the testing strategy. If the user agrees:

  - If there is an AGENTS.md file present in the project, update it with any
    changes you've made to the testing strategy.

  - If there is no AGENTS.md file, create a new file (docs/testing.md) with
    a description of the testing strategy, including the commands needed to
    run every type of test and where the screenshot reference files live.
    Also create a new AGENTS.md file in the root and create a link to
    docs/testing.md.
